  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

## Reproduce
CPU-only, works on Windows, macOS and Linux. Run everything from this folder.
```
conda create -n patchsloth python=3.11 && conda activate patchsloth
pip install -r requirements.txt && pip install -e .     # GPU box: also requirements-gpu.txt
python scripts/01_download.py        # or: bash scripts/01_download.sh
python scripts/02_build_dataset.py
python scripts/03_baselines.py
python scripts/07_tabpfn_bump.py --model hgb      # or --model tabpfn (GPU)
patchsloth feed build                # HGB-only second-opinion feed -> feed/
pytest -q
```
The M1 numbers are in `results/m1_reproduction.md`. Decisions and their reasons are in `DECISIONS.md`.

## Use
```
patchsloth scan path/to/package-lock.json --no-llm   # or requirements.txt, or a project directory
patchsloth cve CVE-2025-5889
patchsloth serve                                     # web page + API on http://127.0.0.1:8080
patchsloth costs
```
`--no-llm` makes no paid calls: the bump probability comes from HistGBT and the report from a template. When
`PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY` is set in `.env`, Ultramarine 1 Flash writes the report. A guardrail checks every CVE
ID and number in its report against the input, and falls back to the template if the check fails.
If [osv-scanner](https://github.com/google/osv-scanner) is installed and `OSV_SCANNER_LOCAL_DB_CACHE_DIRECTORY` points
to its offline DB, it is used for matching; otherwise a built-in matcher runs over the GitHub Advisory Database.

See `PLAN.md` for the full build plan.

# Patch Sloth

NIST no longer analyses every CVE. Since April 2026, many CVEs are marked **Deferred**, and the only severity score they carry comes from the CNA, the organisation that reported the vulnerability (often the vendor itself). In the years when NIST still reviewed those scores, it changed about 4 in 10 of them, and it raised them more often than it lowered them.

Patch Sloth reads your lockfile and finds the vulnerabilities NIST never checked. For each one it says whether an independent reviewer would likely rate it higher, and it writes you a one-minute patch list.

## Stack
- **Tinker:** fine-tunes Qwen3-8B to produce the "second opinion" CVSS vector.
- **TabPFN:** predicts the probability that the severity band gets bumped up.
- **DigitalOcean:** serves the model, the app, and the weekly scan.
- **Ultramarine 1 Flash:** writes the report.

## Reproduce
```
pip install -r requirements.txt
bash scripts/01_download.sh
python scripts/02_build_dataset.py
python scripts/03_baselines.py
python scripts/07_tabpfn_bump.py --model hgb      # or --model tabpfn (GPU)
python scripts/04_make_tinker_data.py && python scripts/05_tinker_train.py --dry_run
```
See `PLAN.md` for the full build plan and the current results.

## Data and licences
- **NVD**, via the [fkie-cad mirror](https://github.com/fkie-cad/nvd-json-data-feeds): public domain.
- **CISA KEV:** public domain.
- **GitHub Advisory Database:** CC-BY 4.0.
- **EPSS:** FIRST.org.
- **TabPFN 2.5:** non-commercial licence. This project is used for research and hackathon purposes only.

Predictions are estimates for triage. They are not official scores.

input.new_string:
## Reproduce
CPU-only, works on Windows, macOS and Linux. Run everything from this folder.
```
conda create -n patchsloth python=3.11 && conda activate patchsloth
pip install -r requirements.txt && pip install -e .     # GPU box: also requirements-gpu.txt
python scripts/01_download.py        # or: bash scripts/01_download.sh
python scripts/02_build_dataset.py
python scripts/03_baselines.py
python scripts/07_tabpfn_bump.py --model hgb      # or --model tabpfn (GPU)
patchsloth feed build                # HGB-only second-opinion feed -> feed/
pytest -q
```
The M1 numbers are in `results/m1_reproduction.md`. Decisions and their reasons are in `DECISIONS.md`.

## Use
```
patchsloth scan path/to/package-lock.json --no-llm   # or requirements.txt, or a project directory
patchsloth cve CVE-2025-5889
patchsloth serve                                     # web page + API on http://127.0.0.1:8080
patchsloth costs
```
`--no-llm` makes no paid calls: the bump probability comes from HistGBT and the report from a template. When
`PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY` is set in `.env`, Ultramarine 1 Flash writes the report. A guardrail checks every CVE
ID and number in its report against the input, and falls back to the template if the check fails.
If [osv-scanner](https://github.com/google/osv-scanner) is installed and `OSV_SCANNER_LOCAL_DB_CACHE_DIRECTORY` points
to its offline DB, it is used for matching; otherwise a built-in matcher runs over the GitHub Advisory Database.

See `PLAN.md` for the full build plan.

content.text:
All three milestones are committed on `master`. Tests pass: 102 with the osv-scanner offline DB available, or 100 plus 2 skipped without it. Ruff is clean, and every decision is logged in `DECISIONS.md`.

**M0 (`df80f27`)**
- The package now has the layout from §6, and the scripts are thin entry points.
- Tests cover CVSS scoring, the label rule (including the NaN regression), leakage and train/serve parity, and output parsing.
- `pip` installed pandas 3.0, which stores missing values as NaN. The NaN regression test runs through a DataFrame, and it already caught one new NaN bug in my own feature code.

**M1 (`24175a9`)**: the numbers match the spec, well within ±2%. Details are in `results/m1_reproduction.md`.

| | Spec | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Dataset rows | 239,058 | identical, same splits and rates |
| HistGBT test PR-AUC | 0.58 [0.56–0.60] | 0.580 [0.561–0.599] |
| HistGBT precision in top 10% | 0.53 | 0.529 |
| Logistic regression test PR-AUC | 0.45 | 0.449 |

**M5 on CPU (`04a6ccc`)**
- **Scanning:** osv-scanner 2.7.0 installed via scoop, and it agrees exactly with my fallback matcher on the fixtures (18/18 npm and 19/19 PyPI CVEs). It must run with `--offline`; without that flag it sends your dependency list to deps.dev to resolve transitive packages.
- **Feed:** 57,603 unanalysed CVEs scored with HistGBT. Train and serve features match on real data (max difference 1e-16).
- **Fixtures:** built from real packages (lodash, ajv, vue 2, gradio, requests and others) and include 9 currently Deferred CVEs.
- **Report:** Ultramarine is checked against its official docs: tool calling works, prices match the spec, and reasoning can't be turned off, so I use the lowest setting. With no key, it falls back to the template.
- **Also done:** priority rules, the guardrail, the API, the CLI and the web page, checked end to end against a live server.
- **Post material:** 2,105 Deferred CVEs appear in npm/PyPI advisories in the GitHub Advisory DB.

**Decisions I need from you**
1. **τ (the flagging threshold).** The spec's rule gives τ = 0.072. On 2026 test data that flags with only 0.29 precision instead of 0.5, because late-2025 validation data has twice the 2026 rate of severity bumps. In the demo report, a CVE at p=0.13 shows as "likely under-rated". I did not tune on test. The options are:
   - (a) keep it and say so in the post;
   - (b) adjust using the 2026 base rate, which reads one number from test labels;
   - (c) only flag the top 10% of scores, which gives 0.53 precision on test.
2. **A rule I added to priority.** For CVEs NVD has already analysed, the priority now uses the higher of the CNA's and NVD's severity. For example, lodash CVE-2026-4800 is HIGH from the CNA and CRITICAL from NVD. Is that OK?

**[HUMAN] steps**
- **Ultramarine key:** put `PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY=...` in `patch-sloth/.env`; don't paste it into this chat. Nothing is blocked without it: the template report is used.
- **Optional, for the osv-scanner path:** set `OSV_SCANNER_LOCAL_DB_CACHE_DIRECTORY` to `<repo>\patch-sloth\osv-db`. The DB is already downloaded and gitignored.
- **Tomorrow on the GPU box:** sign the TabPFN licence and add the Tinker key (§16 items 5 and 7). Then run `pip install -r requirements-gpu.txt`.

**Things to know**
- Windows Defender blocks 6 GitHub advisories that quote exploit code. The scanner skips and lists them, so you don't need to change antivirus settings. It also makes the one-time index build take about 7 minutes.
- The dataset only covers CVE IDs from 2021 onward. Older CVEs show as "not in the feed" unless you pass `--fetch-missing`.
- `scripts/04` still needs to set aside the 10k extra training rows for stacking (§9.1) before tomorrow's Tinker run. I didn't do that tonight because it was outside tonight's scope.

Sources: [Ultramarine quickstart](https://docs.paperinstruments.com/docs/ultramarine), [Chat Completions](https://docs.paperinstruments.com/docs/ultramarine/chat-completions), [Billing](https://docs.paperinstruments.com/docs/ultramarine/billing), [Wavect overview](https://wavect.io/blog/ultramarine-1-flash-api-document-workflows.md), [OrcaRouter release note](https://www.orcarouter.ai/it/blog/ultramarine-1-flash-release)

"""Task A: LoRA SFT of Qwen3-8B on Tinker, then greedy eval on val/test.
Needs: pip install tinker tinker-cookbook ; export TINKER_API_KEY=...
NOTE: written against the Tinker low-level API (ServiceClient / forward_backward / optim_step /
sampling client). Check names against the current docs before the first run - run with --dry_run first.
Usage: python scripts/05_tinker_train.py --epochs 1 --eval_n 8000
"""
import argparse
import json
import random

import tinker
from tinker import types
from tinker_cookbook import renderers
from tinker_cookbook.tokenizer_utils import get_tokenizer

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--base", default="Qwen/Qwen3-8B")
ap.add_argument("--rank", type=int, default=32)
ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-4)
ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)
ap.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=1)
ap.add_argument("--eval_n", type=int, default=8000, help="examples per eval split (cost control)")
ap.add_argument("--dry_run", action="store_true")
a = ap.parse_args()

tok = get_tokenizer(a.base)
renderer = renderers.get_renderer("qwen3", tok)  # chat template matching the base model

def to_datum(msgs):
    tokens, weights = renderer.build_supervised_example(msgs)  # weights=1 only on assistant tokens
    tokens, weights = list(tokens), list(weights)
    return types.Datum(model_input=types.ModelInput.from_ints(tokens[:-1]),
                       loss_fn_inputs=dict(weights=weights[1:], target_tokens=tokens[1:]))

train = [json.loads(l) for l in open("data/tinker/train.jsonl")]
if a.dry_run:
    train = train[:128]
svc = tinker.ServiceClient()
tc = svc.create_lora_training_client(base_model=a.base, rank=a.rank)
log = open("results/tinker_train_log.jsonl", "a")
step = 0
for ep in range(a.epochs):
    random.Random(ep).shuffle(train)
    for i in range(0, len(train), a.batch):
        batch = [to_datum(x["messages"]) for x in train[i:i + a.batch]]
        fb = tc.forward_backward(batch, "cross_entropy")
        opt = tc.optim_step(types.AdamParams(learning_rate=a.lr * (1 - i / len(train))))
        r = fb.result(); opt.result()
        step += 1
        if step % 10 == 0:
            loss = sum(float(x) for x in r.metrics.values()) if hasattr(r, "metrics") else None
            log.write(json.dumps({"step": step, "epoch": ep, "metrics": getattr(r, "metrics", {})}, default=str) + "\n"); log.flush()
            print("step", step, getattr(r, "metrics", ""))

sampler = tc.save_weights_and_get_sampling_client(name="patch-sloth-taskA")
params = types.SamplingParams(max_tokens=48, temperature=0.0, stop=renderer.get_stop_sequences())

def predict(split, client, tag):
    rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(f"data/tinker/{split}.jsonl")]
    rows = rows[: (64 if a.dry_run else a.eval_n)]
    futures = []
    for x in rows:
        prompt = renderer.build_generation_prompt(x["messages"][:-1])
        futures.append((x["cve"], client.sample(prompt=prompt, num_samples=1, sampling_params=params)))
    with open(f"results/llm_preds_{tag}_{split}.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for cve, fut in futures:
            seq = fut.result().sequences[0].tokens
            f.write(json.dumps({"cve": cve, "text": tok.decode(seq)}) + "\n")

base_sampler = svc.create_sampling_client(base_model=a.base)  # zero-shot baseline, same prompt
for split in ["val", "test"]:
    predict(split, sampler, "ft")
    predict(split, base_sampler, "base")
print("saved preds -> results/llm_preds_*.jsonl ; now run scripts/06_eval_llm.py")

"""Build chat-format JSONL for Tinker SFT (Task A). Target = NVD-final vector as compact JSON.
Keeps prompts short (~250 tokens) so Qwen3-8B training stays inside the $10 credit.
Also reserves `stack_train`: train rows OUTSIDE the SFT set, drawn from the same recency-weighted pool,
for out-of-SFT LLM predictions used to train the stacked bump classifier (SPEC §9.1/§9.2).
val/test are shuffled (seed 0) so that 05's first-eval_n rows are a random subsample.
Usage: python scripts/04_make_tinker_data.py --n_train 30000 --n_stack 10000"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from patchsloth.llm.prompt import SYSTEM, prompt, target  # noqa: E402  (shared with serving)

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--n_train", type=int, default=30000)
ap.add_argument("--n_stack", type=int, default=10000)
a = ap.parse_args()
df = pd.read_parquet("data/cves.parquet")
out = Path("data/tinker"); out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

tr = df[df.split == "train"]
# oversample recent + changed examples so the model sees enough disagreements
recent = tr[tr.published >= "2024-01-01"]
pool = pd.concat([recent, tr.drop(recent.index).sample(frac=0.3, random_state=0)]).sample(frac=1, random_state=0)
if len(pool) < a.n_train + a.n_stack:
    sys.exit(f"pool has {len(pool)} rows < n_train + n_stack = {a.n_train + a.n_stack}")
splits = {
    "train": pool.iloc[:a.n_train],
    "stack_train": pool.iloc[a.n_train:a.n_train + a.n_stack],
    "val": df[df.split == "val"].sample(frac=1, random_state=0),
    "test": df[df.split == "test"].sample(frac=1, random_state=0),
}
assert not set(splits["train"].cve) & set(splits["stack_train"].cve), "stack_train overlaps the SFT set"
for split, d in splits.items():
    with open(out / f"{split}.jsonl", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for r in d.itertuples():
            f.write(json.dumps({"cve": r.cve, "messages": [
                {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM},
                {"role": "user", "content": prompt(r)},
                {"role": "assistant", "content": target(r)}]}) + "\n")
    print(split, len(d), "bump rate", round(d.bump_up.astype(float).mean(), 3),
          "published", d.published.min(), "->", d.published.max())
# rough token estimate: 4 chars/token (05 --dry_run counts real tokens)
n = sum(len(line) for line in open(out / "train.jsonl", encoding="utf-8")) / 4
print(f"~{n/1e6:.1f}M train tokens/epoch -> ~${n/1e6*0.44:.2f} per epoch on Qwen3-8B at $0.44/M")

"""Print installed tinker / tinker_cookbook versions and the signatures 05 depends on (no network)."""
import importlib.metadata as md
import inspect

for p in ("tinker", "tinker-cookbook"):
    print(p, md.version(p))

import tinker  # noqa: E402
from tinker import types  # noqa: E402

for name in ("create_lora_training_client", "create_sampling_client"):
    print("ServiceClient." + name, inspect.signature(getattr(tinker.ServiceClient, name)))
TC = tinker.TrainingClient
for name in ("forward_backward", "optim_step", "save_weights_and_get_sampling_client", "save_weights_for_sampler"):
    print("TrainingClient." + name, inspect.signature(getattr(TC, name)) if hasattr(TC, name) else "MISSING")
print("SamplingClient.sample", inspect.signature(tinker.SamplingClient.sample))
for t in ("Datum", "ModelInput", "AdamParams", "SamplingParams"):
    cls = getattr(types, t)
    fields = getattr(cls, "model_fields", None)
    print(t, list(fields) if fields else inspect.signature(cls))
print("ModelInput.from_ints", hasattr(types.ModelInput, "from_ints"))

from tinker_cookbook import renderers  # noqa: E402

print("get_renderer", inspect.signature(renderers.get_renderer))
src = inspect.getsource(renderers.get_renderer)
print("renderer names:", [ln.strip() for ln in src.splitlines() if "==" in ln or "case" in ln][:40])
from tinker_cookbook import tokenizer_utils  # noqa: E402

print("get_tokenizer", inspect.signature(tokenizer_utils.get_tokenizer))
R = renderers.Renderer
for m in ("build_supervised_example", "build_generation_prompt", "get_stop_sequences", "parse_response"):
    print("Renderer." + m, inspect.signature(getattr(R, m)) if hasattr(R, m) else "MISSING")
try:
    from tinker_cookbook.supervised import data as sd
    print("supervised.data:", [n for n in dir(sd) if "datum" in n.lower()])
except Exception as e:
    print("supervised.data import:", e)
try:
    from tinker_cookbook import weights
    print("weights:", [n for n in dir(weights) if not n.startswith("_")])
except Exception as e:
    print("weights import:", e)

- "Supported Models" is shown as "28+" on the index, but the models table lists 36 rows. Qwen/Qwen3-8B is in the table.

1. CLIENT CREATION
- Quickstart and cheatsheet: `import tinker`; `service_client = tinker.ServiceClient()` with comment "# Entry point — reads TINKER_API_KEY from environment".
- ServiceClient signature (API ref): `class tinker.ServiceClient(user_metadata=None, project_id=None, display_name=None, base_url=None, api_key=None, default_headers_overrides=None, **kwargs)`. api_key "Defaults to the `TINKER_API_KEY` environment variable, then to the stored credentials."
- Cheatsheet: `training_client = service_client.create_lora_training_client(base_model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B", rank=32)`
- Full signature: `create_lora_training_client(base_model, rank=32, seed=None, train_mlp=True, train_attn=True, train_unembed=True, user_metadata=None, optimizer=None)` returns TrainingClient. Async variant: `create_lora_training_client_async()`.
- Sampling: `service_client.create_sampling_client(model_path=None, base_model=None, retry_config=None, record_stability_info=False)`. Raises ValueError if neither model_path nor base_model is given. Cheatsheet: `service_client.create_sampling_client(base_model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B")`.
- Also: `training_client.get_tokenizer()` (cheatsheet) and `sampling_client.get_tokenizer()` (SamplingClient API ref, returns PreTrainedTokenizer).
- Quickstart uses `tinker.ServiceClient(display_name="my-first-sft")`, `create_lora_training_client_async(base_model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B", rank=16)`.

Is Qwen/Qwen3-8B supported? Yes. The models table row is quoted in the models page summary: "Qwen3-8B | Qwen/Qwen3-8B | 32K | 8B | 8B | Dense | Hybrid". The Tinker ID is `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`. The quickstart does not mention Qwen3-8B; it uses Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B.

2. forward_backward (TrainingClient)
- Signature: `forward_backward(data, loss_fn, loss_fn_config=None)`. Returns: "APIFuture containing the forward/backward outputs, loss, and gradients".
- Cheatsheet: `fwdbwd_future = await training_client.forward_backward_async(data=[datum], loss_fn="cross_entropy")`; `fwdbwd_result = await fwdbwd_future.result_async()`; `print(f"Loss: {fwdbwd_result.loss}")`.
- Non-async form: `training_client.forward_backward(training_data, "cross_entropy")`, then `fwdbwd_future.result()`.
- Other loss strings in cheatsheet: "importance_sampling", "ppo", "cispo", "dro"; custom: `forward_backward_custom_async(data, my_loss_fn)`.
- The result field is `.loss` (quoted in cheatsheet and API ref example). Field names `loss_fn_outputs` and `metrics` and the key `'loss:sum'`: NOT FOUND in pages read. ForwardBackwardOutput page was not read.
- Also `forward(data, loss_fn, loss_fn_config=None)` exists (no gradients).

3. Datum for cross-entropy SFT (cheatsheet, "Prepare training data")
- "A `Datum` is a single training example. It contains input tokens, target tokens, and per-token loss weights (0 = ignore, 1 = compute loss). Position `i` of the input predicts token `i + 1`"
- Code:
  full_sequence = prompt_tokens + completion_tokens
  n_prefix = len(prompt_tokens) - 1
  datum = types.Datum(
      model_input=types.ModelInput.from_ints(tokens=full_sequence[:-1]),
      loss_fn_inputs=dict(
          weights=[0.0] * n_prefix + [1.0] * len(completion_tokens),  # 0 for prompt, 1 for completion
          target_tokens=full_sequence[1:],  # shifted by 1 from input
      )
  )
- So loss_fn_inputs keys are `weights` and `target_tokens`. In the cheatsheet they are plain Python lists of float and int. Whether TensorData or numpy is also accepted is NOT VERIFIED (Datum and TensorData pages not read).
- Note: the renderer's build_supervised_example returns weights as a torch.Tensor (see section 7). The cheatsheet passes lists. Convert with .tolist() if needed (inference).
- RL variant: target_tokens, logprobs, advantages keys.

- Signature: `optim_step(optim_params=None, adam_params=None)`. Returns "APIFuture containing optimizer step response". adam_params is "a legacy alias and cannot be combined with `optim_params`" [summary].
- Cheatsheet: `await training_client.optim_step_async(types.AdamParams(learning_rate=1e-4))` then `await optim_future.result_async()`. Quickstart: `tinker.AdamParams(learning_rate=2e-4)`.
- AdamParams fields (verbatim field names): learning_rate (float, "Learning rate for the optimizer"), beta1 (float), beta2 (float), eps (float, "Term added to the denominator to improve numerical stability"), weight_decay (float, "Uses decoupled weight decay."), grad_clip_norm (float, "0.0 means no clipping."). """Task A: LoRA SFT of Qwen3-8B on Tinker, then greedy predictions for val/test (ft + base zero-shot)
and stack_train (ft only, out-of-SFT rows for stacking, SPEC §9.2).
API names VERIFIED 2026-10-23 against tinker 0.34.0 / tinker-cookbook 0.5.7 and tinker-docs (see DECISIONS.md).

Every token is counted locally before any paid call; the run aborts if the estimate exceeds --budget.
Usage:
  python scripts/05_tinker_train.py --dry_run          # 128 train examples, 64 eval rows per split
  python scripts/05_tinker_train.py --estimate_only    # exact token counts + projected cost, no API calls
  python scripts/05_tinker_train.py                    # full run: 1 epoch, eval_n=8000, n_stack=10000
  python scripts/05_tinker_train.py --model_path tinker://.../sampler_weights/... --skip_train   # eval only
"""
import argparse
import json
import random
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import Future
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from patchsloth import config, costs  # noqa: E402

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--base", default=config.BASE_MODEL)
ap.add_argument("--renderer", default=config.TINKER_RENDERER)
ap.add_argument("--rank", type=int, default=32)
ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-4)
ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)
ap.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=1)
ap.add_argument("--eval_n", type=int, default=8000, help="rows per eval split (val/test are pre-shuffled by 04)")
ap.add_argument("--n_stack", type=int, default=10000, help="stack_train rows to predict with the fine-tuned model")
ap.add_argument("--max_tokens", type=int, default=48)
ap.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=64, help="sample requests in flight")
ap.add_argument("--budget", type=float, default=config.TINKER_BUDGET_USD)
ap.add_argument("--dry_run", action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--estimate_only", action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--skip_train", action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--model_path", default=None, help="tinker://... sampler weights to evaluate (with --skip_train)")
a = ap.parse_args()

import tinker  # noqa: E402
from tinker import types  # noqa: E402
from tinker_cookbook import renderers  # noqa: E402
from tinker_cookbook.renderers import TrainOnWhat  # noqa: E402
from tinker_cookbook.supervised.data import conversation_to_datum  # noqa: E402
from tinker_cookbook.tokenizer_utils import get_tokenizer  # noqa: E402

P = config.TINKER_PRICE
TAG = "_dryrun" if a.dry_run else ""
n_train_rows = 128 if a.dry_run else None
n_eval = 64 if a.dry_run else a.eval_n
n_stack = 64 if a.dry_run else a.n_stack

tok = get_tokenizer(a.base)
renderer = renderers.get_renderer(a.renderer, tok)


def load(split, n=None):
    rows = [json.loads(line) for line in open(f"data/tinker/{split}.jsonl", encoding="utf-8")]
    return rows[:n] if n else rows


def to_datum(msgs):
    # loss only on the assistant JSON; per-example mean reduction (cookbook SFT default)
    return conversation_to_datum(msgs, renderer, max_length=None, train_on_what=TrainOnWhat.LAST_ASSISTANT_MESSAGE)


def prompt_of(x):
    return renderer.build_generation_prompt(x["messages"][:-1])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- exact token accounting
train = load("train", n_train_rows)
data = [to_datum(x["messages"]) for x in train]
train_tokens = sum(d.model_input.length for d in data) * a.epochs
eval_sets = [("val", "ft", n_eval), ("test", "ft", n_eval), ("val", "base", n_eval), ("test", "base", n_eval),
             ("stack_train", "ft", n_stack)]
prompts = {s: [prompt_of(x) for x in load(s, n)] for s, _, n in eval_sets}
prefill_tokens = sum(sum(p.length for p in prompts[s]) for s, _, _ in eval_sets)
n_samples = sum(len(prompts[s]) for s, _, _ in eval_sets)

           sample_tokens_max=n_samples * a.max_tokens)
est["usd_train"] = train_tokens * P["train"] / 1e6
est["usd_prefill"] = prefill_tokens * P["prefill"] / 1e6  # upper bound: ignores cached-prefill discount
est["usd_sample_max"] = est["sample_tokens_max"] * P["sample"] / 1e6
est["usd_total_max"] = est["usd_train"] + est["usd_prefill"] + est["usd_sample_max"]
print("ESTIMATE", json.dumps({k: round(v, 4) if isinstance(v, float) else v for k, v in est.items()}))
if a.estimate_only:
    sys.exit(0)
if est["usd_total_max"] > a.budget:
    sys.exit(f"ABORT: estimated ${est['usd_total_max']:.2f} > budget ${a.budget:.2f}")

svc = tinker.ServiceClient()
spent = {"train": 0.0, "prefill": 0.0, "sample": 0.0}
run = dict(base=a.base, renderer=a.renderer, rank=a.rank, lr=a.lr, batch=a.batch, epochs=a.epochs,
           n_train=len(train), dry_run=a.dry_run, estimate=est)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- training
if a.skip_train:
    if not a.model_path:
        sys.exit("--skip_train needs --model_path")
    ft_path = a.model_path
else:
    tc = svc.create_lora_training_client(base_model=a.base, rank=a.rank, seed=0)
    log = open(f"results/tinker_train_log{TAG}.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8")
    steps_per_epoch = (len(data) + a.batch - 1) // a.batch
    total, step, t0 = steps_per_epoch * a.epochs, 0, time.time()
    for ep in range(a.epochs):
        order = list(range(len(data)))
        random.Random(ep).shuffle(order)
        for i in range(0, len(order), a.batch):
            batch = [data[j] for j in order[i:i + a.batch]]
            lr = a.lr * (1 - step / total)  # linear decay to 0 over the whole run
            fb = tc.forward_backward(batch, "cross_entropy")
            opt = tc.optim_step(types.AdamParams(learning_rate=lr))
            r = fb.result()
            opt.result()
            step += 1
            ntok = sum(d.model_input.length for d in batch)
            spent["train"] += ntok * P["train"] / 1e6
            if step % 10 == 0 or a.dry_run or step == total:
                rec = dict(step=step, epoch=ep, lr=lr, tokens=ntok, metrics=r.metrics, usd_train=spent["train"],
                           elapsed_s=round(time.time() - t0, 1))
                log.write(json.dumps(rec, default=float) + "\n")
                log.flush()
                print("step", step, "/", total, r.metrics, f"${spent['train']:.3f}")
    costs.log("tinker", a.base, int(train_tokens), 0, time.time() - t0, spent["train"], task=f"sft{TAG}",
              train_tokens=int(train_tokens), steps=step)
    ft_path = tc.save_weights_for_sampler(name=f"patchsloth-taskA{TAG or '-final'}").result().path
    print("saved sampler weights:", ft_path)
run["ft_path"] = ft_path
Path(f"results/tinker_run{TAG}.json").write_text(json.dumps(run, indent=1, default=float))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- sampling
params = types.SamplingParams(max_tokens=a.max_tokens, temperature=0.0, stop=renderer.get_stop_sequences())
clients = {"ft": svc.create_sampling_client(model_path=ft_path),
           "base": svc.create_sampling_client(base_model=a.base)}  # zero-shot baseline, same prompt + renderer


def predict(split, tag, n):
    rows = load(split, n)
    t0, out = time.time(), [None] * len(rows)
    pre = cached = gen = 0
    inflight: list[tuple[int, Future]] = []

    def drain(k):
        nonlocal pre, cached, gen
        while len(inflight) > k:
            i, fut = inflight.pop(0)
            res = fut.result()
            seq = res.sequences[0]
            out[i] = seq.tokens
            pre += prompts[split][i].length
            cached += getattr(res, "prompt_cache_hit_tokens", 0) or 0
            gen += len(seq.tokens)

    for i in range(len(rows)):
        inflight.append((i, clients[tag].sample(prompt=prompts[split][i], num_samples=1, sampling_params=params)))
        drain(a.concurrency)
    drain(0)
    with open(f"results/llm_preds_{tag}_{split}{TAG}.jsonl", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for x, toks in zip(rows, out):
            f.write(json.dumps({"cve": x["cve"], "text": tok.decode(toks)}) + "\n")
    usd_pre = ((pre - cached) * P["prefill"] + cached * P["prefill_cached"]) / 1e6
    usd_gen = gen * P["sample"] / 1e6
    spent["prefill"] += usd_pre
    spent["sample"] += usd_gen
    costs.log("tinker", a.base, pre, gen, time.time() - t0, usd_pre + usd_gen, task=f"sample_{tag}_{split}{TAG}",
              cached_input_tokens=cached, n=len(rows))
    print(f"{tag} {split}: n={len(rows)} prefill={pre} (cached {cached}) gen={gen} "
          f"mean_gen={gen / max(len(rows), 1):.1f} ${usd_pre + usd_gen:.4f}")
    return dict(n=len(rows), prefill=pre, cached=cached, gen=gen)


run["sampling"] = {f"{tag}_{s}": predict(s, tag, n) for s, tag, n in eval_sets}
run["spent_usd"] = {**spent, "total": sum(spent.values())}
Path(f"results/tinker_run{TAG}.json").write_text(json.dumps(run, indent=1, default=float))
print("SPENT", json.dumps({k: round(v, 4) for k, v in run["spent_usd"].items()}))
print("saved preds -> results/llm_preds_*; now run scripts/06_eval_llm.py" + (" --dry_run" if a.dry_run else ""))

and stack_train (ft only, out-of-SFT rows for stacking, SPEC §9.2).

import json
import random
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import Future
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from patchsloth import config, costs  # noqa: E402

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--base", default=config.BASE_MODEL)
ap.add_argument("--renderer", default=config.TINKER_RENDERER)
ap.add_argument("--rank", type=int, default=32)
ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-4)
ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)
ap.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=1)
ap.add_argument("--eval_n", type=int, default=8000, help="rows per eval split (val/test are pre-shuffled by 04)")
ap.add_argument("--n_stack", type=int, default=10000, help="stack_train rows to predict with the fine-tuned model")
ap.add_argument("--max_tokens", type=int, default=48)
ap.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=64, help="sample requests in flight")
ap.add_argument("--budget", type=float, default=config.TINKER_BUDGET_USD)
ap.add_argument("--dry_run", action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--estimate_only", action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--skip_train", action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--model_path", default=None, help="tinker://... sampler weights to evaluate (with --skip_train)")
a = ap.parse_args()

import tinker  # noqa: E402
from tinker import types  # noqa: E402
from tinker_cookbook import renderers  # noqa: E402
from tinker_cookbook.renderers import TrainOnWhat  # noqa: E402
from tinker_cookbook.supervised.data import conversation_to_datum  # noqa: E402
from tinker_cookbook.tokenizer_utils import get_tokenizer  # noqa: E402

n_train_rows = 128 if a.dry_run else None
n_eval = 64 if a.dry_run else a.eval_n
n_stack = 64 if a.dry_run else a.n_stack

tok = get_tokenizer(a.base)
renderer = renderers.get_renderer(a.renderer, tok)


def load(split, n=None):
    rows = [json.loads(line) for line in open(f"data/tinker/{split}.jsonl", encoding="utf-8")]
    return rows[:n] if n else rows


def to_datum(msgs):
    # loss only on the assistant JSON; per-example mean reduction (cookbook SFT default)
    return conversation_to_datum(msgs, renderer, max_length=None, train_on_what=TrainOnWhat.LAST_ASSISTANT_MESSAGE)


def prompt_of(x):

train = load("train", n_train_rows)
data = [to_datum(x["messages"]) for x in train]
train_tokens = sum(d.model_input.length for d in data) * a.epochs

est["usd_sample_max"] = est["sample_tokens_max"] * P["sample"] / 1e6
est["usd_total_max"] = est["usd_train"] + est["usd_prefill"] + est["usd_sample_max"]

if est["usd_total_max"] > a.budget:
    sys.exit(f"ABORT: estimated ${est['usd_total_max']:.2f} > budget ${a.budget:.2f}")

svc = tinker.ServiceClient()
spent = {"train": 0.0, "prefill": 0.0, "sample": 0.0}
run = dict(base=a.base, renderer=a.renderer, rank=a.rank, lr=a.lr, batch=a.batch, epochs=a.epochs,

    for ep in range(a.epochs):
        order = list(range(len(data)))
        random.Random(ep).shuffle(order)
        for i in range(0, len(order), a.batch):

def predict(split, tag, n):

    pre = cached = gen = 0
    inflight: list[tuple[int, Future]] = []

    def drain(k):
        nonlocal pre, cached, gen
        while len(inflight) > k:
            i, fut = inflight.pop(0)
            res = fut.result()
            seq = res.sequences[0]
            out[i] = seq.tokens

    usd_gen = gen * P["sample"] / 1e6
    spent["prefill"] += usd_pre
    spent["sample"] += usd_gen
    costs.log("tinker", a.base, pre, gen, time.time() - t0, usd_pre + usd_gen, task=f"sample_{tag}_{split}{TAG}",

    print(f"{tag} {split}: n={len(rows)} prefill={pre} (cached {cached}) gen={gen} "
          f"mean_gen={gen / max(len(rows), 1):.1f} ${usd_pre + usd_gen:.4f}")

print("SPENT", json.dumps({k: round(v, 4) for k, v in run["spent_usd"].items()}))
print("saved preds -> results/llm_preds_*; now run scripts/06_eval_llm.py" + (" --dry_run" if a.dry_run else ""))

"""Task A: LoRA SFT of Qwen3-8B on Tinker, then greedy eval on val/test.
Needs: pip install tinker tinker-cookbook ; export TINKER_API_KEY=...
NOTE: written against the Tinker low-level API (ServiceClient / forward_backward / optim_step /
sampling client). Check names against the current docs before the first run - run with --dry_run first.
Usage: python scripts/05_tinker_train.py --epochs 1 --eval_n 8000
"""
import argparse
import json
import random

import tinker
from tinker import types
from tinker_cookbook import renderers
from tinker_cookbook.tokenizer_utils import get_tokenizer

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--base", default="Qwen/Qwen3-8B")
ap.add_argument("--rank", type=int, default=32)
ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-4)
ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)
ap.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=1)
ap.add_argument("--eval_n", type=int, default=8000, help="examples per eval split (cost control)")
ap.add_argument("--dry_run", action="store_true")
a = ap.parse_args()

tok = get_tokenizer(a.base)
renderer = renderers.get_renderer("qwen3", tok)  # chat template matching the base model

def to_datum(msgs):
    tokens, weights = renderer.build_supervised_example(msgs)  # weights=1 only on assistant tokens
    tokens, weights = list(tokens), list(weights)
    return types.Datum(model_input=types.ModelInput.from_ints(tokens[:-1]),
                       loss_fn_inputs=dict(weights=weights[1:], target_tokens=tokens[1:]))

train = [json.loads(l) for l in open("data/tinker/train.jsonl")]
if a.dry_run:
    train = train[:128]
svc = tinker.ServiceClient()
tc = svc.create_lora_training_client(base_model=a.base, rank=a.rank)
log = open("results/tinker_train_log.jsonl", "a")
step = 0
for ep in range(a.epochs):
    random.Random(ep).shuffle(train)
    for i in range(0, len(train), a.batch):
        batch = [to_datum(x["messages"]) for x in train[i:i + a.batch]]
        fb = tc.forward_backward(batch, "cross_entropy")
        opt = tc.optim_step(types.AdamParams(learning_rate=a.lr * (1 - i / len(train))))
        r = fb.result(); opt.result()
        step += 1
        if step % 10 == 0:
            loss = sum(float(x) for x in r.metrics.values()) if hasattr(r, "metrics") else None
            log.write(json.dumps({"step": step, "epoch": ep, "metrics": getattr(r, "metrics", {})}, default=str) + "\n"); log.flush()
            print("step", step, getattr(r, "metrics", ""))

sampler = tc.save_weights_and_get_sampling_client(name="patch-sloth-taskA")
params = types.SamplingParams(max_tokens=48, temperature=0.0, stop=renderer.get_stop_sequences())

def predict(split, client, tag):
    rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(f"data/tinker/{split}.jsonl")]
    rows = rows[: (64 if a.dry_run else a.eval_n)]
    futures = []
    for x in rows:
        prompt = renderer.build_generation_prompt(x["messages"][:-1])
        futures.append((x["cve"], client.sample(prompt=prompt, num_samples=1, sampling_params=params)))
    with open(f"results/llm_preds_{tag}_{split}.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for cve, fut in futures:
            seq = fut.result().sequences[0].tokens
            f.write(json.dumps({"cve": cve, "text": tok.decode(seq)}) + "\n")

base_sampler = svc.create_sampling_client(base_model=a.base)  # zero-shot baseline, same prompt
for split in ["val", "test"]:
    predict(split, sampler, "ft")
    predict(split, base_sampler, "base")
print("saved preds -> results/llm_preds_*.jsonl ; now run scripts/06_eval_llm.py")

spent = {"train": 0.0, "prefill": 0.0, "sample": 0.0}

           n_train=len(train), dry_run=a.dry_run, estimate=est)

    ft_path = a.model_path
else:
    tc = svc.create_lora_training_client(base_model=a.base, rank=a.rank, seed=0)
    log = open(f"results/tinker_train_log{TAG}.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8")
    steps_per_epoch = (len(data) + a.batch - 1) // a.batch
    total, step, t0 = steps_per_epoch * a.epochs, 0, time.time()
    for ep in range(a.epochs):
        order = list(range(len(data)))
        random.Random(ep).shuffle(order)
        for i in range(0, len(order), a.batch):
            batch = [data[j] for j in order[i:i + a.batch]]

            opt.result()

                log.flush()

Path(f"results/tinker_run{TAG}.json").write_text(json.dumps(run, indent=1, default=float))

clients = {"ft": svc.create_sampling_client(model_path=ft_path),
           "base": svc.create_sampling_client(base_model=a.base)}  # zero-shot baseline, same prompt + renderer


def predict(split, tag, n):
    rows = load(split, n)
    t0, out = time.time(), [None] * len(rows)
    pre = cached = gen = 0
    inflight: list[tuple[int, Future]] = []

    def drain(k):
        nonlocal pre, cached, gen
        while len(inflight) > k:
            i, fut = inflight.pop(0)
            res = fut.result()
            seq = res.sequences[0]
            out[i] = seq.tokens

            gen += len(seq.tokens)

    spent["sample"] += usd_gen

run["spent_usd"] = {**spent, "total": sum(spent.values())}
Path(f"results/tinker_run{TAG}.json").write_text(json.dumps(run, indent=1, default=float))

"""Task A: LoRA SFT of Qwen3-8B on Tinker, then greedy predictions for val/test (ft + base zero-shot)
and stack_train (ft only, out-of-SFT rows for stacking, SPEC §9.2).
API names VERIFIED 2026-10-23 against tinker 0.34.0 / tinker-cookbook 0.5.7 and tinker-docs (see DECISIONS.md).

Every token is counted locally before any paid call; the run aborts if the estimate exceeds --budget.
Usage:
  python scripts/05_tinker_train.py --dry_run          # 128 train examples, 64 eval rows per split
  python scripts/05_tinker_train.py --estimate_only    # exact token counts + projected cost, no API calls
  python scripts/05_tinker_train.py                    # full run: 1 epoch, eval_n=8000, n_stack=10000
  python scripts/05_tinker_train.py --model_path tinker://.../sampler_weights/... --skip_train   # eval only
"""
import argparse
import json
import random
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import Future
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from patchsloth import config, costs  # noqa: E402

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--base", default=config.BASE_MODEL)
ap.add_argument("--renderer", default=config.TINKER_RENDERER)
ap.add_argument("--rank", type=int, default=32)
ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-4)
ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)
ap.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=1)
ap.add_argument("--eval_n", type=int, default=8000, help="rows per eval split (val/test are pre-shuffled by 04)")
ap.add_argument("--n_stack", type=int, default=10000, help="stack_train rows to predict with the fine-tuned model")
ap.add_argument("--max_tokens", type=int, default=48)
ap.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=64, help="sample requests in flight")
ap.add_argument("--budget", type=float, default=config.TINKER_BUDGET_USD)
ap.add_argument("--dry_run", action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--estimate_only", action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--skip_train", action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--model_path", default=None, help="tinker://... sampler weights to evaluate (with --skip_train)")
a = ap.parse_args()

import tinker  # noqa: E402
from tinker import types  # noqa: E402
from tinker_cookbook import renderers  # noqa: E402
from tinker_cookbook.renderers import TrainOnWhat  # noqa: E402
from tinker_cookbook.supervised.data import conversation_to_datum  # noqa: E402
from tinker_cookbook.tokenizer_utils import get_tokenizer  # noqa: E402

P = config.TINKER_PRICE
TAG = "_dryrun" if a.dry_run else ""
n_train_rows = 128 if a.dry_run else None
n_eval = 64 if a.dry_run else a.eval_n
n_stack = 64 if a.dry_run else a.n_stack

tok = get_tokenizer(a.base)
renderer = renderers.get_renderer(a.renderer, tok)


def load(split, n=None):
    rows = [json.loads(line) for line in open(f"data/tinker/{split}.jsonl", encoding="utf-8")]
    return rows[:n] if n else rows


def to_datum(msgs):

    return conversation_to_datum(msgs, renderer, max_length=None, train_on_what=TrainOnWhat.LAST_ASSISTANT_MESSAGE)


def prompt_of(x):
    return renderer.build_generation_prompt(x["messages"][:-1])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- exact token accounting
train = load("train", n_train_rows)
data = [to_datum(x["messages"]) for x in train]
train_tokens = sum(d.model_input.length for d in data) * a.epochs
eval_sets = [("val", "ft", n_eval), ("test", "ft", n_eval), ("val", "base", n_eval), ("test", "base", n_eval),
             ("stack_train", "ft", n_stack)]
prompts = {s: [prompt_of(x) for x in load(s, n)] for s, _, n in eval_sets}
prefill_tokens = sum(sum(p.length for p in prompts[s]) for s, _, _ in eval_sets)
n_samples = sum(len(prompts[s]) for s, _, _ in eval_sets)

           sample_tokens_max=n_samples * a.max_tokens)
est["usd_train"] = train_tokens * P["train"] / 1e6

est["usd_sample_max"] = est["sample_tokens_max"] * P["sample"] / 1e6
est["usd_total_max"] = est["usd_train"] + est["usd_prefill"] + est["usd_sample_max"]
print("ESTIMATE", json.dumps({k: round(v, 4) if isinstance(v, float) else v for k, v in est.items()}))
if a.estimate_only:
    sys.exit(0)
if est["usd_total_max"] > a.budget:

svc = tinker.ServiceClient()
spent = {"train": 0.0, "prefill": 0.0, "sample": 0.0}
run = dict(base=a.base, renderer=a.renderer, rank=a.rank, lr=a.lr, batch=a.batch, epochs=a.epochs,
           n_train=len(train), dry_run=a.dry_run, estimate=est)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- training
if a.skip_train:

    ft_path = a.model_path

    tc = svc.create_lora_training_client(base_model=a.base, rank=a.rank, seed=0)
    log = open(f"results/tinker_train_log{TAG}.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8")
    steps_per_epoch = (len(data) + a.batch - 1) // a.batch
    total, step, t0 = steps_per_epoch * a.epochs, 0, time.time()
    for ep in range(a.epochs):
        order = list(range(len(data)))
        random.Random(ep).shuffle(order)
        for i in range(0, len(order), a.batch):
            batch = [data[j] for j in order[i:i + a.batch]]
            lr = a.lr * (1 - step / total)  # linear decay to 0 over the whole run
            fb = tc.forward_backward(batch, "cross_entropy")
            opt = tc.optim_step(types.AdamParams(learning_rate=lr))
            r = fb.result()
            opt.result()
            step += 1
            ntok = sum(d.model_input.length for d in batch)
            spent["train"] += ntok * P["train"] / 1e6
            if step % 10 == 0 or a.dry_run or step == total:
                rec = dict(step=step, epoch=ep, lr=lr, tokens=ntok, metrics=r.metrics, usd_train=spent["train"],
                           elapsed_s=round(time.time() - t0, 1))
                log.write(json.dumps(rec, default=float) + "\n")
                log.flush()
                print("step", step, "/", total, r.metrics, f"${spent['train']:.3f}")
    costs.log("tinker", a.base, int(train_tokens), 0, time.time() - t0, spent["train"], task=f"sft{TAG}",
              train_tokens=int(train_tokens), steps=step)
    ft_path = tc.save_weights_for_sampler(name=f"patchsloth-taskA{TAG or '-final'}").result().path
    print("saved sampler weights:", ft_path)
run["ft_path"] = ft_path
Path(f"results/tinker_run{TAG}.json").write_text(json.dumps(run, indent=1, default=float))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- sampling
params = types.SamplingParams(max_tokens=a.max_tokens, temperature=0.0, stop=renderer.get_stop_sequences())
clients = {"ft": svc.create_sampling_client(model_path=ft_path),
           "base": svc.create_sampling_client(base_model=a.base)}  # zero-shot baseline, same prompt + renderer


def predict(split, tag, n):
    rows = load(split, n)
    t0, out = time.time(), [None] * len(rows)
    pre = cached = gen = 0
    inflight: list[tuple[int, Future]] = []

    def drain(k):
        nonlocal pre, cached, gen
        while len(inflight) > k:
            i, fut = inflight.pop(0)
            res = fut.result()
            seq = res.sequences[0]
            out[i] = seq.tokens
