| Model | PR-AUC, mean of 3 seeds | 95% CI (seed 0) | seed sd |
|---|---|---|---|
| HGB, 30k subsample | 0.617 | 0.600–0.634 | 0.003 |
| HGB, 50k subsample | 0.618 | 0.594–0.630 | 0.004 |
| HGB, all 80k | 0.626 | 0.610–0.644 | 0.001 |
| HGB, all 80k, no early stopping | 0.631 | 0.613–0.647 | 0.000 |
| HGB, train 2024+ only (40,204 rows) | 0.609 | 0.590–0.626 | 0.003 |
| TabPFN, 50k subsample | 0.637 | 0.617–0.652 | 0.001 |
| TabPFN, train 2024+ only (40,204 rows) | 0.631 | 0.616–0.649 | 0.002 |

- **The anomaly was a mislabel, not recency.** M2's "HGB all train" (0.579) was a 10k-row model. HGB on all 80k rows
  scores 0.626, and 30k is not better than 80k: 30k − 80k is −0.005 to −0.013, with the CI below 0 in 2 of 3 seeds.
- **Recency does not help.** Training only on 2024+ is significantly worse for HGB (−0.012 to −0.020, all seeds), and
  no better for TabPFN (−0.002 to −0.008).
- Turning HGB's early stopping off adds +0.003 to +0.006 (significant in 2 of 3 seeds), which is not enough to call.

## 6. Serving (`results/serving_{stack,tabpfn,hgb}.json`, release `feed-2026-10-23`, data as of 2026-10-23)

**Feed model: the stacked/gated system** (`17_stacked_model.py`). The stack is TabPFN-3.5 with fine-tuned-LLM features,
trained on the 10k out-of-SFT `stack_train` rows (seed 0). Its predictions are identical to the M4 seed-0 stack
(max |Δp| = 0.0), so the gate threshold t = 0.668 from §4 applies unchanged. **Fallbacks:** TabPFN-3.5 (50k,
tabular only) for unanalysed CVEs without an LLM vector (none in this build), and HGB on all 80k train rows (CPU) for
CVEs not in the feed. Each fallback has its own bands. The stack is not significantly better than TabPFN at ranking
(§2). It is served because the gate needs it, and the gate is the part that beats copy-CNA (§4).

**LLM vectors for the unanalysed CVEs** (`16_tinker_unanalysed.py`, approved ~$2.6 with a hard stop at $3.5):
58,457 CVEs, fine-tuned Qwen3-8B on Tinker, greedy decoding, same prompt and renderer as M3. **Spend $2.571** ($0.003
smoke test + $2.568 main run, 59% of prefill tokens cached), logged in `results/costs.jsonl`. The hard stop was not
hit, and json_valid is 1.000. That is $0.044 per 1k CVEs, in line with §3.

Users see a **band**, never a raw probability. The cut-offs are label-free quantiles of the stack's p_bump over the
49,272 Deferred CVEs. Isotonic calibration (`p_bump_calibrated`) is fitted on the last 3 months of val (rows with
LLM predictions, n = 3,878).

| Band | Rule (stack cut-off) | Share of Deferred | Share of 2026 eval test | Observed bump rate, 2026 eval test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| likely | p ≥ τ = 0.725 (top 10%) | 10.0% | 4.7% | **0.747** (281/376) |
| possible | p ≥ 0.333 (top 25%) | 15.0% | 9.3% | 0.294 |
| unlikely | the rest | 75.0% | 86.0% | 0.038 |

- τ_high = top 5% of Deferred = 0.868. On the 2026 eval rows it flags 2.4%, with precision 0.916 and recall 0.230.
- Gate: the predicted vector is the LLM vector only when p ≥ 0.668, otherwise the CNA vector. On 2026 eval test this
  overrides 6.0% of rows, with severity accuracy 0.899 vs copy-CNA 0.880 (+2.0 [1.5, 2.5]). In the feed it overrides
  **11.5%** of unanalysed CVEs (6,732; severity changes for 6,718). Deferred CVEs score higher than 2026 test, as
  the 10% vs 4.7% "likely" shares show. That is the same population shift seen in M1.
- Feed: 58,457 unanalysed CVEs (Deferred 49,272, Awaiting Analysis 6,604, Received 1,902, Undergoing Analysis 679),
  all scored by the stack. Bands: likely 5,179, possible 8,105, unlikely 45,173. Isotonic maps the top 102 rows to
  1.0; the band is the honest summary (observed ~0.75 in "likely" on 2026).
- TabPFN-only component (`serving_tabpfn.json`; τ 0.722, τ_high 0.847; "likely" band in §8) and HGB fallback (τ 0.703,
  τ_high 0.845) numbers are unchanged.
- **Distribution:** `feed/` is gitignored. The feed (`second_opinion.parquet`, `latest.csv`, `meta.json`) and the HGB
  fallback model (`bump_hgb.joblib`) are assets of the GitHub release `feed-2026-10-23`. At start-up the API
  downloads the newest `feed-*` release (`PATCHSLOTH_FEED_DOWNLOAD=0` turns this off). It skips the download if
  the tag is already local, and if GitHub is unreachable it serves the local feed.

## 7. Headline claims (approved wording, 2026-10-23)

> "When Patch Sloth said 'likely under-rated', NIST had raised the score 75% of the time (281/376) vs a 9.5% base
> rate."

Source: the served combined model's (stack, §6) "likely" band (label-free cut-off: top 10% of Deferred scores) on
the 8,000 2026 evaluation test rows (`results/serving_stack.json`, `test_eval_rows`). It flags 4.7% of those rows.
The TabPFN-only component's figure is in §8.

> Gated override: with a threshold tuned on all of 2025-H2, letting the LLM rewrite CNA vectors is **worse** than
> copying the CNA on 2026 (−2.1 points). Tuned on the most recent 3 months, it is **better**: +2.0 points
> [1.5, 2.5]. The model was the same; the lesson is drift.

For context: if instead the top 10% of 2026 test CVEs are flagged, precision is 0.558 (TabPFN-50k) to 0.574 (HGB-80k).
The fine-tuned LLM alone does not beat copying the CNA on 2026 (0.859 vs 0.880).

## 8. TabPFN is about sample efficiency, not accuracy (`results/learning_curve.png`, `m4_tables.md`)

Same 8,000 eval test rows; 3 seeds (the seed draws the training subsample and seeds the model).

| n_train | TabPFN-3.5 PR-AUC (mean, seed sd) | HistGBT PR-AUC (mean, seed sd) | TabPFN − HGB at equal n, per seed [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5k | 0.602 (0.008) | 0.534 (0.019) | +0.073 [+0.052, +0.093]; +0.080 [+0.056, +0.103]; +0.052 [+0.034, +0.068]: **TabPFN better** |
| 10k | 0.614 (0.002) | 0.564 (0.005) | +0.047 [+0.029, +0.065]; +0.054 [+0.032, +0.074]; +0.051 [+0.032, +0.071]: **TabPFN better** |
| 30k | 0.625 (0.002) | 0.612 (0.004) | +0.013 [−0.002, +0.027]; +0.017 [+0.001, +0.031]; +0.009 [−0.006, +0.022]: no significant difference |
| 50k / 80k | 0.631 (50k) | 0.627 (all 80,098) | see below |

**TabPFN at n vs HGB on all 80k rows (paired, per seed):**

| TabPFN at | Seed 0 | Seed 1 | Seed 2 | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5k | −0.024 [−0.042, −0.008] | −0.036 [−0.054, −0.019] | −0.015 [−0.033, +0.001] | no significant difference under the every-seed rule, but significantly **lower** in 2 of 3 seeds |
| 10k | −0.014 [−0.029, −0.000] | −0.015 [−0.032, −0.001] | −0.009 [−0.025, +0.006] | no significant difference (lower in 2 of 3 seeds) |
| 30k | −0.004 [−0.018, +0.010] | −0.004 [−0.018, +0.010] | +0.001 [−0.015, +0.015] | no significant difference |
| 50k | −0.003 [−0.016, +0.011] | +0.007 [−0.008, +0.021] | +0.009 [−0.008, +0.024] | no significant difference |

What the post can say:
- **With little data, TabPFN wins clearly.** At 5k and 10k training rows it beats HGB trained on the same rows by
  +0.05 to +0.08 PR-AUC, significant in every seed.
- **TabPFN on 5k rows gets 96% of the way to HGB on 80k rows** (0.602 vs 0.627), with 1/16 of the labelled data and
  no tuning. It is not *equal*: the gap is significant in 2 of 3 seeds. From 30k rows on, the two are level.
- With all the data, HGB catches up. TabPFN is not more accurate here; it gets there with far fewer labels.
- **TabPFN-only component** (50k, tabular features; the fallback for unanalysed CVEs without an LLM vector): its
  "likely" band is confirmed 78% of the time (254/327) on the same 8,000 2026 eval rows, vs a 9.5% base rate
  (`results/serving_tabpfn.json`). The headline (§7) uses the served combined model's 75% (281/376).

## 9. What went wrong

**1. The "HistGBT" baseline was trained on 10k rows, and nobody noticed for three milestones.**
`scripts/07_tabpfn_bump.py` has `--n_train` (default 10,000) so that TabPFN's context size can be set. The same default
silently applied to `--model hgb`, and the README ran `07 --model hgb` without the flag. As a result, the SPEC §9.2
bar ("HistGBT 0.58"), the M1 reproduction, M2's "TabPFN beats full-train HGB, CIs don't overlap" and the served
fallback model were all a 10k-row HGB.
*How it was caught:* M2 had flagged an "anomaly": HGB refitted on a 30k subsample (0.618) beat "HGB on all 80k rows"
(0.579). M4 re-ran the anomaly check with 3 seeds and an explicit config table. `hgb_full` on all 80,098 rows scored
0.626, not 0.579, and the gap traced straight to the default. With the real baseline, TabPFN's accuracy edge mostly
disappears (§2). The project's TabPFN story became sample efficiency (§8), not accuracy.
*Fixes:* the M2 write-up is corrected in place with a note; `07` documents the default; serve-time models are built by
`15`, which has no subsample default; every M4 config states its training rows.

**2. The NaN label bug (scaffold, before this repo's sessions).** The label rule (SPEC §8.2: NVD's vector if NVD wrote
one, else the CNA's) was first written with truthiness checks (`nvd_vector or cna_vector`). pandas stores missing
strings as NaN, which is truthy, so for rows NVD had accepted unchanged (no NVD-written score) the rule returned NaN
and those rows silently lost their labels. The labelled set was 115,092 rows, every one of them a row where NVD wrote
its own score: a biased sample of mostly disagreements. After the fix it is 122,459 rows.
*How it was caught:* on 2026-10-21, during the first dataset build, in a separate chat session before Entire was
enabled. The sanity check showed 100% of labelled rows had an NVD-written score, contradicting the earlier profiling
(roughly half had none), and the 2026 "vector changed" rate came out at 93% instead of the expected ~20%.
*Fix:* `label_vector` uses `isinstance(x, str)` and lives in `patchsloth/data/nvd.py` as a pure function.
`tests/test_label_rule.py` checks that None, NaN, `np.nan` and `pd.NA` never produce a label, both directly and
through a DataFrame, because pandas 3.0 turns missing strings into NaN.

**3. A test that passed on Windows and failed on Linux.** `tests/test_scan.py` failed on the GPU workstation with a
different "fixed" version for brace-expansion (1.1.12 vs 1.1.20). I first blamed the fresh advisory-database clone
and logged it that way. That was wrong: the fixtures use a pinned advisory snapshot.
*Real cause:* `scan.build_index` walked the advisories with `rglob`, whose order is the filesystem's (alphabetical on
NTFS, hash order on ext4). The test then kept the *last* finding per package, and a package can match several
advisories with different fixes.
*Fix:* the index is built from `sorted(rglob(...))`, and the test checks that the expected fix is among the package's
fixes. The product was never wrong (each CVE row keeps its own advisory's fix), but its output order depended on the
OS.

**Also:** the Ultramarine frontier baseline was first compared on 1k rows against Qwen on 8k rows (§3 fixes it); and a
threshold tuned on older val months does not transfer to 2026 (M1 τ, §4), which is now a finding rather than a bug.

213	## 9. What went wrong
214	
215	**1. The "HistGBT" baseline was trained on 10k rows, and nobody noticed for three milestones.**
216	`scripts/07_tabpfn_bump.py` has `--n_train` (default 10,000) so that TabPFN's context size can be set. The same default
217	silently applied to `--model hgb`, and the README ran `07 --model hgb` without the flag. As a result, the SPEC §9.2
218	bar ("HistGBT 0.58"), the M1 reproduction, M2's "TabPFN beats full-train HGB, CIs don't overlap" and the served
219	fallback model were all a 10k-row HGB.
220	*How it was caught:* M2 had flagged an "anomaly": HGB refitted on a 30k subsample (0.618) beat "HGB on all 80k rows"
221	(0.579). M4 re-ran the anomaly check with 3 seeds and an explicit config table. `hgb_full` on all 80,098 rows scored
222	0.626, not 0.579, and the gap traced straight to the default. With the real baseline, TabPFN's accuracy edge mostly
223	disappears (§2). The project's TabPFN story became sample efficiency (§8), not accuracy.
224	*Fixes:* the M2 write-up is corrected in place with a note; `07` documents the default; serve-time models are built by
225	`15`, which has no subsample default; every M4 config states its training rows.
226	
227	**2. The NaN label bug (scaffold, before this repo's sessions).** The label rule (SPEC §8.2: NVD's vector if NVD wrote
228	one, else the CNA's) was first written with truthiness checks (`nvd_vector or cna_vector`). pandas stores missing
229	strings as NaN, which is truthy, so for rows NVD had accepted unchanged (no NVD-written score) the rule returned NaN
230	and those rows silently lost their labels. The labelled set was 115,092 rows, every one of them a row where NVD wrote
231	its own score: a biased sample of mostly disagreements. After the fix it is 122,459 rows.
232	*How it was caught:* on 2026-10-21, during the first dataset build, in a separate chat session before Entire was
233	enabled. The sanity check showed 100% of labelled rows had an NVD-written score, contradicting the earlier profiling
234	(roughly half had none), and the 2026 "vector changed" rate came out at 93% instead of the expected ~20%.
235	*Fix:* `label_vector` uses `isinstance(x, str)` and lives in `patchsloth/data/nvd.py` as a pure function.
236	`tests/test_label_rule.py` checks that None, NaN, `np.nan` and `pd.NA` never produce a label, both directly and
237	through a DataFrame, because pandas 3.0 turns missing strings into NaN.
238	
239	**3. A test that passed on Windows and failed on Linux.** `tests/test_scan.py` failed on the GPU workstation with a
240	different "fixed" version for brace-expansion (1.1.12 vs 1.1.20). I first blamed the fresh advisory-database clone
241	and logged it that way. That was wrong: the fixtures use a pinned advisory snapshot.
242	*Real cause:* `scan.build_index` walked the advisories with `rglob`, whose order is the filesystem's (alphabetical on
243	NTFS, hash order on ext4). The test then kept the *last* finding per package, and a package can match several
244	advisories with different fixes.
245	*Fix:* the index is built from `sorted(rglob(...))`, and the test checks that the expected fix is among the package's
246	fixes. The product was never wrong (each CVE row keeps its own advisory's fix), but its output order depended on the
247	OS.
248	
249	**Also:** the Ultramarine frontier baseline was first compared on 1k rows against Qwen on 8k rows (§3 fixes it); and a
250	threshold tuned on older val months does not transfer to 2026 (M1 τ, §4), which is now a finding rather than a bug.

# Final results (M3 + M4)

**Evaluation snapshot: NVD data as of 2026-10-21T14:41Z** (`results/data_as_of.txt`). Every headline comparison uses
the same rows: the val (2025-H2) and test (2026) CVEs that have a fine-tuned LLM prediction, 8,000 each (the M3
`eval_n` rows). The workstation's data is from 2026-10-23, and all 75 M3 metrics reproduce exactly on it, so these
rows' labels are unchanged (DECISIONS.md). Newer data is used for serving only. All CIs are 95% bootstrap intervals;
"better" means the paired-bootstrap CI of the difference (1,000 resamples) excludes 0 **for every one of 3 seeds**.
Generated tables: `results/m4_tables.md` (from `scripts/13_final_table.py`), `results/frontier_1k.json`,
`results/gated_override.json`.

## 1. Task A (M3): base vs fine-tuned Qwen3-8B (`results/llm_{val,test}.json`, n = 8,000 each)

| Split | Model | JSON valid | Severity acc [95% CI] | Bump precision | Bump recall | Bump F1 | McNemar vs copy-CNA (model-only / copy-only correct, p) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| val | copy-CNA | — | 0.722 | 0 | 0 | 0 | — |
| val | base zero-shot | 1.000 | 0.710 [0.699–0.719] | 0.189 | 0.018 | 0.033 | 28 / 129, p = 1e-15 (copy-CNA better) |
| val | **fine-tuned** | 1.000 | **0.869 [0.861–0.876]** | 0.818 | 0.842 | 0.830 | 1,642 / 469, p = 2e-143 (**fine-tune better**) |
| test | copy-CNA | — | **0.880** | 0 | 0 | 0 | — |
| test | base zero-shot | 0.9998 | 0.865 [0.857–0.872] | 0.252 | 0.069 | 0.108 | 47 / 166, p = 6e-16 (copy-CNA better) |
| test | fine-tuned | 1.000 | 0.859 [0.851–0.866] | 0.519 | 0.604 | 0.559 | 520 / 688, p = 2e-6 (**copy-CNA better**) |

Cost (Tinker, `results/costs.jsonl`): SFT $3.37 one-off; inference $0.045 per 1k CVEs (fine-tuned) and $0.063 per 1k
(base, longer answers). Total for the full run: $5.53, plus $0.055 for the dry run.

## 2. Task B: bump classifier, all models on the same 8,000 test rows (base rate 0.095)

| Model (training rows) | PR-AUC, mean of 3 seeds | 95% CI (seed 0) | ROC-AUC | Precision top 10% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| copy-CNA (never flags) | 0.095 | — | — | — |
| Fine-tuned Qwen3-8B alone (score delta as the ranking) | 0.404 | 0.366–0.444 | 0.783 | 0.506 |
| TF-IDF + logistic regression (all train) | 0.426 | 0.391–0.470 | 0.848 | 0.432 |
| HistGBT (10k stack_train) | 0.574 | 0.536–0.609 | 0.891 | 0.514 |
| TabPFN-3.5 (10k stack_train) | 0.609 | 0.574–0.645 | 0.901 | 0.543 |
| HistGBT + LLM features (10k stack_train) | 0.609 | 0.573–0.643 | 0.894 | 0.541 |
| TabPFN-3.5 + LLM features (10k stack_train) | 0.621 | 0.584–0.655 | 0.901 | 0.552 |
| HistGBT (all 80,098 train) | 0.627 | 0.596–0.664 | 0.910 | 0.574 |
| TabPFN-3.5 (50k train subsample) | **0.631** | 0.592–0.662 | 0.911 | 0.558 |

As a yes/no flag, the fine-tuned LLM has precision 0.519 and recall 0.604, flagging 11.0% of rows. Val numbers are in
`m4_tables.md`; there every model except the LLM alone and LR scores 0.91–0.93.

**Paired comparisons (test rows, ΔPR-AUC per seed [95% CI])**

| A vs B | Seed 0 | Seed 1 | Seed 2 | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TabPFN (50k) vs HGB (same 50k) | +0.023 [+0.008, +0.038] | +0.014 [−0.001, +0.029] | +0.018 [+0.002, +0.032] | no significant difference |
| TabPFN (50k) vs HGB (all 80k) | −0.003 [−0.016, +0.011] | +0.007 [−0.008, +0.021] | +0.009 [−0.008, +0.024] | no significant difference |
| Stacked vs TabPFN, same 10k rows | +0.011 [−0.003, +0.024] | +0.014 [+0.002, +0.027] | +0.012 [−0.001, +0.026] | no significant difference |
| Stacked vs TabPFN (50k) | −0.007 [−0.025, +0.010] | −0.012 [−0.029, +0.005] | −0.011 [−0.028, +0.007] | no significant difference |
| Stacked vs fine-tuned LLM alone | +0.216 [+0.189, +0.243] | +0.218 [+0.191, +0.243] | +0.218 [+0.190, +0.243] | **stacked better** |
| HGB + LLM vs HGB, same 10k rows | +0.035 [+0.017, +0.053] | +0.035 [+0.017, +0.053] | +0.035 [+0.017, +0.053] | **HGB + LLM better** |

What this supports:
- On the 8k evaluation rows, **TabPFN-3.5 is not significantly better than a well-trained HGB**; its advantage is
  sample efficiency (§8). It is ahead of HGB on
  the same 50k rows in 2 of 3 seeds, and level with HGB on all 80k rows.
  Secondary (all 31,198 test rows of the serving data, `m4_tables.md`): TabPFN-50k beats HGB-80k in all 3 seeds,
  by +0.008 to +0.014. That set is newer data and is not the headline.
- **LLM features help HGB significantly (+0.035), but not TabPFN** (+0.011 to +0.014; significant in 1 of 3 seeds).
  The stack trains on only 10k rows, because those are the only out-of-SFT train rows with LLM predictions.
- The stack is much better than the fine-tuned LLM on its own at ranking likely bumps (+0.22).
- The SPEC §9.2 "HistGBT 0.58" bar was a **10k-row** HGB (07's default `--n_train`). Every model trained on 30k+ rows
  beats it.

## 3. Same 1,000 test rows as Ultramarine (`results/frontier_1k.json`, base rate 0.102)

The Ultramarine subsample is a subset of the 8k eval rows. Before this, `llm_test.json` compared Ultramarine on 1k rows
with Qwen on 8k rows; here every model is scored on the same 1,000.

| Model | Severity acc [95% CI] | Exact vector | Score MAE | Bump P / R / F1 | McNemar vs copy-CNA | $ per 1k CVEs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| copy-CNA | **0.874 [0.853–0.897]** | 0.801 | 0.344 | 0 / 0 / 0 | — | 0 |
| base Qwen3-8B zero-shot | 0.865 [0.844–0.887] | 0.774 | 0.358 | 0.30 / 0.07 / 0.11 | 7 / 16, p = 0.10 | 0.063 (Tinker) |
| fine-tuned Qwen3-8B | 0.861 [0.839–0.883] | 0.776 | 0.353 | 0.56 / 0.54 / 0.55 | 65 / 78, p = 0.32 | 0.045 (Tinker) + $3.37 training |
| TF-IDF + LR | 0.833 [0.810–0.855] | 0.702 | 0.429 | 0.47 / 0.63 / 0.54 | 69 / 110, p = 0.003 | 0 (CPU) |
| Ultramarine 1 Flash zero-shot | 0.795 [0.771–0.822] | 0.650 | 0.525 | 0.29 / 0.28 / 0.29 | 32 / 111, p = 7e-11 | 0.092 |

Bump ranking on the same 1k rows (PR-AUC, mean of 3 seeds): TabPFN-50k 0.659, HGB-80k 0.658, TabPFN (10k stack_train)
0.640, stacked 0.623. With n = 1,000 these do not separate. TabPFN and HGB run locally (GPU / CPU) with no metered
cost; TabPFN-50k takes about 6 min per 43k rows scored on the RTX PRO 4000.

## 4. Gated override: use the LLM vector only when the stack is confident (`results/gated_override.{json,png}`)

Final vector = fine-tuned LLM vector if stacked p_bump ≥ t, else the CNA vector. t is swept and chosen on val labels
only (max severity accuracy). Two val rules were coded before the run: all of val, and the last 3 months of val (the
window SPEC §9.2 uses for τ). Test is reported at the chosen t, with a paired bootstrap of severity accuracy vs
copy-CNA (0.8795 on these rows).

| t chosen on | Seed | t | Test override rate | Test severity acc | Δ vs copy-CNA [95% CI] | Test bump P / R |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all val | 0 / 1 / 2 | ≈ 0 (override ~all) | 99.7% | 0.859 | −0.021 [−0.030, −0.013] | 0.52 / 0.60 |
| last 3 months of val | 0 | 0.668 | 6.0% | **0.899** | **+0.020 [+0.015, +0.025]** | 0.71 / 0.44 |
| last 3 months of val | 1 | 0.685 | 5.4% | **0.900** | **+0.020 [+0.015, +0.025]** | 0.73 / 0.41 |
| last 3 months of val | 2 | 0.666 | 5.9% | **0.899** | **+0.019 [+0.014, +0.024]** | 0.71 / 0.43 |
| *(exploratory: t picked on test labels)* | 0 | — | — | 0.900 | +0.020 | — |

**The drift lesson.** Both rules were specified before the run, and both use only val labels:

- **Stale calibration loses.** Tuned on all of 2025-H2 val (bump rate 0.23), the gate learns "trust the LLM almost
  always". On 2026 (bump rate 0.095) that is significantly **worse** than copying the CNA: −2.1 points
  [−3.0, −1.3], in all 3 seeds.
- **A recent window wins.** Tuned on the last 3 months of val, the gate overrides only the ~6% of CVEs the stack is
  most confident about. On 2026 that **beats copy-CNA by +2.0 points [1.5, 2.5]** of severity accuracy in all
  3 seeds, almost matching the best threshold picked with hindsight on test.
- Same model, same features; only the tuning window differs. NVD's behaviour moved in 2026 (it changes far fewer CNA
  vectors), so a threshold tuned on older decisions over-corrects. This is the same drift as the τ finding in M1.
- In the product since M4 sign-off: the feed uses this gate (t = 0.668) on Tinker vectors for every unanalysed CVE
  (§6).

## 5. HGB "anomaly" and recency (all 31,198 test rows, serving data)

| Model | PR-AUC, mean of 3 seeds | 95% CI (seed 0) | seed sd |
|---|---|---|---|
| HGB, 30k subsample | 0.617 | 0.600–0.634 | 0.003 |
| HGB, 50k subsample | 0.618 | 0.594–0.630 | 0.004 |
| HGB, all 80k | 0.626 | 0.610–0.644 | 0.001 |
| HGB, all 80k, no early stopping | 0.631 | 0.613–0.647 | 0.000 |

## 9. What went wrong

**1. The "HistGBT" baseline was trained on 10k rows, and nobody noticed for three milestones.**
`scripts/07_tabpfn_bump.py` has `--n_train` (default 10,000) so that TabPFN's context size can be set. The same default
silently applied to `--model hgb`, and the README ran `07 --model hgb` without the flag. As a result, the SPEC §9.2
bar ("HistGBT 0.58"), the M1 reproduction, M2's "TabPFN beats full-train HGB, CIs don't overlap" and the served
fallback model were all a 10k-row HGB.
*How it was caught:* M2 had flagged an "anomaly": HGB refitted on a 30k subsample (0.618) beat "HGB on all 80k rows"
(0.579). M4 re-ran the anomaly check with 3 seeds and an explicit config table. `hgb_full` on all 80,098 rows scored
0.626, not 0.579, and the gap traced straight to the default. With the real baseline, TabPFN's accuracy edge mostly
disappears (§2). The project's TabPFN story became sample efficiency (§8), not accuracy.
*Fixes:* the M2 write-up is corrected in place with a note; `07` documents the default; serve-time models are built by
`15`, which has no subsample default; every M4 config states its training rows.

**2. The NaN label bug (scaffold, before this repo's sessions).** The label rule (SPEC §8.2: NVD's vector if NVD wrote
one, else the CNA's) was first written with truthiness checks (`nvd_vector or cna_vector`). pandas stores missing
strings as NaN, which is truthy, so for rows NVD had accepted unchanged (no NVD-written score) the rule returned NaN
and those rows silently lost their labels. The labelled set was 115,092 rows, every one of them a row where NVD wrote
its own score: a biased sample of mostly disagreements. After the fix it is 122,459 rows.
*How it was caught:* on 2026-10-21, during the first dataset build, in a separate chat session before Entire was
enabled. The sanity check showed 100% of labelled rows had an NVD-written score, contradicting the earlier profiling
(roughly half had none), and the 2026 "vector changed" rate came out at 93% instead of the expected ~20%.
*Fix:* `label_vector` uses `isinstance(x, str)` and lives in `patchsloth/data/nvd.py` as a pure function.
`tests/test_label_rule.py` checks that None, NaN, `np.nan` and `pd.NA` never produce a label, both directly and
through a DataFrame, because pandas 3.0 turns missing strings into NaN.

**3. A test that passed on Windows and failed on Linux.** `tests/test_scan.py` failed on the GPU workstation with a
different "fixed" version for brace-expansion (1.1.12 vs 1.1.20). I first blamed the fresh advisory-database clone
and logged it that way. That was wrong: the fixtures use a pinned advisory snapshot.
*Real cause:* `scan.build_index` walked the advisories with `rglob`, whose order is the filesystem's (alphabetical on
NTFS, hash order on ext4). The test then kept the *last* finding per package, and a package can match several
advisories with different fixes.
*Fix:* the index is built from `sorted(rglob(...))`, and the test checks that the expected fix is among the package's
fixes. The product was never wrong (each CVE row keeps its own advisory's fix), but its output order depended on the
OS.

**Also:** the Ultramarine frontier baseline was first compared on 1k rows against Qwen on 8k rows (§3 fixes it); and a
threshold tuned on older val months does not transfer to 2026 (M1 τ, §4), which is now a finding rather than a bug.

TabPFN@5k vs HGB@80k: −0.015 to −0.036, significantly lower in 2 of 3 seeds. So TabPFN gets ~96% of HGB-80k's PR-AUC from 1/16 of the data, not "equal" · `results/learning_curve.png`, `final_table.md` §8.
- 2026-10-23 · Added "What went wrong" (`final_table.md` §9): the HGB-on-10k mislabel, the NaN label bug and the Windows/Linux `rglob` order test bug. How the NaN bug was caught was supplied by the human (2026-10-21 sanity check: 100% NVD-written labels, 93% 2026 "vector changed"; 115,092 → 122,459 labelled rows).
- 2026-10-23 · Tinker LLM vectors for all 58,457 unanalysed CVEs (`16_tinker_unanalysed.py`; approved ~$2.6, hard stop $3.5; the running stop was set at 3.5 − smoke spend). **Spent $2.571** (smoke $0.003 + main $2.568), hard stop not hit, json_valid 1.000; logged in `results/costs.jsonl` (task `sample_ft_unanalysed`). Rows were sent newest first so that a stop would leave the oldest unscored.
- 2026-10-23 · **Feed model = stacked/gated system**, replacing TabPFN-only (supersedes the "Feed model = TabPFN" and "not in the product yet" entries above). Stack = TabPFN-3.5 + LLM features on the 10k stack_train rows, seed 0, verified identical to the M4 seed-0 stack, so the gate t = 0.668 (last 3 months of val) applies. Bands are recomputed on its own Deferred scores: τ 0.725, τ_high 0.868; "likely" on 2026 eval test is 281/376 = 0.747. Fallbacks: TabPFN (tabular) for rows without an LLM vector, HGB for CVEs not in the feed. The gate overrides 11.5% of the feed vs 6.0% of 2026 test (Deferred scores higher) · `results/serving_stack.json`.
- 2026-10-23 · **Headline = served combined model: 75% (281/376)** (human decision). 78% (254/327) is kept only in `final_table.md` §8, labelled "TabPFN-only component".

At start-up the API downloads the newest `feed-*` release in a background thread (`PATCHSLOTH_FEED_REPO`, `PATCHSLOTH_FEED_DOWNLOAD=0` to disable). It skips the download if `feed/release_tag.txt` already matches, fails soft to the local feed, and `/health` reports `feed_release`. ## 8. Dataset, label rule, splits, leakage rules

### 8.1 `data/cves.parquet` schema

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `cve`, `published` | CVE ID and publication date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) |
| `status` | NVD `vulnStatus` |
| `cna` | `sourceIdentifier` |
| `score_source` | `CNA`, `CISA-ADP` or `other` |
| `description` | English description |
| `cna_vector` | Secondary v3.1 vector. Prefer the CNA's own; fall back to ADP. |
| `nvd_vector` | Primary vector |
| `cna_cwe` | `;`-joined |
| `n_refs`, `ref_github`, `ref_exploitdb` | Reference count and flags |
| `has_v40`, `has_cpe` | Booleans |
| `kev_date` | Date added to KEV, if any |
| `label_vector`, `label_score`, `label_sev` | Label (§8.2), its base score and severity rank |
| `cna_score`, `cna_sev` | CNA base score and severity rank |
| `bump_up` | `label_sev > cna_sev` |
| `vector_changed`, `nvd_own` | Booleans |
| `split` | §8.3 |

### 8.2 Label rule (Task A and Task B)

For a CVE with status Analyzed or Modified **and** a CNA v3.1 vector:
- the label is the NVD Primary vector if NVD wrote one;
- otherwise the label is the CNA vector, because NVD reviewed it and kept it.

**Use `isinstance(x, str)` checks, not truthiness.** A NaN-is-truthy bug already happened once and silently mislabelled about 40% of rows. Keep the regression test in §14.

**Known caveat** (put it in the post): in 2026, NVD writes its own score much less often. Some "kept" labels may reflect lower review effort rather than agreement. Mitigation: report val (2025-H2) and test (2026) separately, and add a sensitivity analysis on Jan–Feb 2024, when NVD wrote its own score for about 91% of CVEs.

### 8.3 Splits (time-based, never random)

| Split | Rule |
|---|---|
| `train` | published before 2025-07-01 |
| `val` | 2025-07-01 to 2025-12-31 |
| `test` | 2026-01-01 onwards |
| `deferred_unlabeled` | status Deferred with a CNA vector. This is the population the product scores. |

Bump-up base rates: train 18%, val 23%, test 9%.

### 8.4 Leakage rules (enforce in `features.py`, test in `tests/test_features.py`)

Never use any of the following as features:
- `status`, because NVD prioritises KEV CVEs
- `nvd_vector`
- NVD's CWE (`weaknesses[type=Primary]`)
- NVD reference tags (NVD adds these during analysis)
- `configurations` / `has_cpe`
- `kev_date` (it is a report field only)

Features must be computable for a Deferred CVE on the day it was published. Fit TF-IDF and SVD vocabularies on `train` only.

## 9. Models: what is trained and what is not

| Component | Trained? | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Copy-CNA baseline | no | — | Predict `cna_vector`. This is the bar to beat. |
| TF-IDF + logistic regression (per field) | yes, CPU | local | EXISTS `03_baselines.py` |
| HistGBT bump classifier | yes, CPU | local | EXISTS `07 --model hgb`. Also the serve-time fallback. |
| Base Qwen3-8B zero-shot | no | Tinker sampling | same prompt as the fine-tune |
| **Qwen3-8B LoRA (Task A)** | **yes** | **Tinker** | §9.1 |
| **TabPFN bump classifier (Task B)** | **in-context, no gradient training** | local 24 GB GPU | §9.2 |
| Ultramarine zero-shot vectors (frontier baseline) | no | Paper Instruments API | 1,000 test CVEs, §10 |
| Ultramarine report writer | no | Paper Instruments API | §11.4 |
| Priority rules | no (thresholds tuned on val) | — | §11.3 |

### 9.1 Task A: Tinker LoRA SFT

**Base model.**
- Use `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`: $0.44/M training tokens, $0.195/M prefill and $0.60/M sampling per the Tinker pricing page on 2026-10-19.
- Fallback: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`.
- Renderer: `qwen3` from `tinker_cookbook.renderers`. **VERIFY** the renderer name for the chosen model, and turn thinking off if the renderer exposes that option.

**Data.**
- Produced by `scripts/04_make_tinker_data.py`.
- Train is 30k examples, oversampled towards 2024+. That is about 7.3M tokens, about $3.2 per epoch.
- **Reserve 10k extra `train` rows outside the SFT set as `stack_train`.** These are needed for honest stacking in §9.2.

**Prompt.** `llm/prompt.py` holds the single shared definition for training and serving. Keep the `SYSTEM` prompt as written in `04`. The user turn contains:
- the CNA ID
- the CNA's CWE
- the CNA vector
- the description, truncated to 1,200 characters

**Target.** Compact JSON `{"AV":..,"AC":..,"PR":..,"UI":..,"S":..,"C":..,"I":..,"A":..}`.

**Hyperparameters.**
- LoRA rank 32, learning rate 2e-4 with linear decay, batch 64, 1 epoch.
- Log the loss every 10 steps to `results/tinker_train_log.jsonl`.

**API.**
- `scripts/05_tinker_train.py` uses `ServiceClient`, `create_lora_training_client`, `forward_backward(..., "cross_entropy")`, `optim_step(AdamParams)`, `save_weights_and_get_sampling_client` and `create_sampling_client`.
- **VERIFY every name against https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai before running.**
- Run `--dry_run` (128 examples) first. **[HUMAN]** supplies `TINKER_API_KEY`.

**Evaluation sampling.**
- Greedy, `max_tokens=48`.
- `eval_n=8000` each for val and test, which costs about $2 in prefill.
- Also predict `stack_train` (10k).
- Parse failures fall back to the CNA vector and are counted in `json_valid`.

**Export for serving.**
1. `tinker_cookbook.weights.download(tinker_path="tinker://<run_id>/sampler_weights/final", output_dir="./adapter")`
2. `weights.build_lora_adapter(base_model=..., adapter_path=..., output_path="./peft_adapter")`
3. `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --enable-lora --lora-modules patchsloth=./peft_adapter --max-model-len 2048`

Source: https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/tutorials/deployment/lora-adapter/

**Budget guard.** Abort if the estimated spend is above $9 (Tinker promo credit is $10). Log the estimated cost before every paid call.

### 9.2 Task B: TabPFN bump classifier and stacking

**Package.**
- Use the latest `tabpfn`. Prior Labs recommends **TabPFN-3.5**: open-weight and free after signing the non-commercial licence at platform.priorlabs.ai **[HUMAN]**.
- **VERIFY** how to select 3.5 weights and what their sample and feature limits are. Fallback is TabPFN-2.5 (Hugging Face `Prior-Labs/tabpfn_2_5`, which is tested up to 50k samples and 2k features).
- Run on the local GPU.

**Features.** `features.py` is shared by training and serving:
- CNA vector fields as ordinal integers
- `cna_score`
- top-40 CNA codes and top-40 CWE codes
- `adp_scored`, `n_refs`, `ref_github`, `ref_exploitdb`, `desc_len`, `has_v40`
- 32-dimensional TF-IDF → SVD text embedding

**Stacked features** (`--with_llm`):
- the fine-tuned LLM's predicted score minus the CNA score
- per-field "LLM changed this field" flags

These must come from **out-of-SFT** predictions (`stack_train`) at training time, never from SFT training rows.

**Training sizes.** Run `n_train` = 5k, 10k, 30k and 50k (within the limits). Plot PR-AUC against `n_train` as the scaling curve.

**Calibration.** Report the Brier score and a reliability plot. If the model is miscalibrated, fit isotonic calibration on the first half of val and report on the second half.

**Threshold τ.**
- Choose it on the **most recent 3 months of val** to match the 2026 base rate. Target: precision ≥ 0.5 in the top-flag set.
- Store τ in `config.py`.

**Output.** `feed/second_opinion.parquet` with `p_bump` for every Deferred, Awaiting Analysis and Received CVE.

**Bars to beat (test, 2026, base rate 0.093):**

| Model | PR-AUC | 95% CI | Precision in top 10% |
|---|---|---|---|
| HistGBT | 0.58 | 0.56–0.60 | 0.53 |
| Logistic regression | 0.45 | — | — |

## 10. Evaluation protocol (results must be reproducible from `results/`)

**Models on the same test rows** (val and test):
- copy-CNA
- TF-IDF + LR
- HistGBT
- TabPFN
- base Qwen zero-shot
- fine-tuned Qwen
- fine-tuned Qwen + TabPFN stack
- Ultramarine zero-shot (1,000-row random test subsample; compare every model on that same subsample too)

**Task A metrics:**
- per-field accuracy
- exact-vector match
- severity accuracy
- score MAE
- `json_valid`
- bump-up precision, recall and F1

**Task B metrics:**
- PR-AUC (**headline**)
- ROC-AUC
- Brier score
- precision@top-10%
- recall at τ

**Uncertainty and significance:**
- 1,000-sample bootstrap 95% CIs for severity accuracy, bump F1 and PR-AUC
- McNemar's test against copy-CNA on severity correctness

**Breakdowns:**
- by CNA (top 15 by volume)
- by CVSS field
- by month of 2026 (shows the drift)

**Error analysis** (`10_error_analysis.py`):
- Sample 20 false-positive bump flags and 20 false negatives. Write them to `results/error_sample.md`, showing the description, CNA vector, NVD vector and our vector.
- **[HUMAN]** reads them and tags each one: *model wrong*, *NVD worst-casing*, *ambiguous description*, or *label noise*.

**Cost table:**
- Tinker training and sampling dollars
- Ultramarine dollars per report and per 1k baseline calls
- DigitalOcean dollars per hour and in total

The headline claim template (fill it in with real numbers; do not oversell):
> "On 2026 CVEs, Patch Sloth's top-10% flags were confirmed by NVD X% of the time vs a 9% base rate."

## 11. Product

### 11.1 CLI (`patchsloth`, built with Typer)

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `scan PATH [--format md\|json] [--no-llm] [--no-report]` | Scan a lockfile or a project directory |
| `cve CVE-ID` | Single-CVE second opinion |
| `feed build [--since DATE]` | Nightly job: rebuild the dataset delta, score unanalysed CVEs, write the feed |
| `serve` | Run the FastAPI app locally |
| `costs` | Summarise `results/costs.jsonl` |

### 11.2 Scanning (`scan.py`)

**Primary path:**

```
osv-scanner scan source --offline --format=json --output-file=<tmp> <dir>
```

- Use the offline DB cache, set by `OSV_SCANNER_LOCAL_DB_CACHE_DIRECTORY`. Download it once with `--offline-vulnerabilities --download-offline-databases`.
- For a single lockfile, **VERIFY** the current flag (v2 uses `-L/--lockfile`).
- Parse the vulnerability IDs and `aliases`, and keep `CVE-*` IDs.
- Keep the package name, installed version and fixed version (if any).

### 11.3 Priority rules (`priority.py`, deterministic, explained in the report)

For each CVE, compute `eff_sev = max(cna_sev, predicted_sev if p_bump ≥ τ else cna_sev)`. Then assign the first matching bucket:

| Bucket | Rule |
|---|---|
| **P0 "Patch now"** | in KEV; **or** EPSS ≥ 0.10; **or** (eff_sev ≥ HIGH **and** p_bump ≥ τ_high **and** a fixed version exists) |
| **P1 "This month"** | eff_sev ≥ HIGH; **or** p_bump ≥ τ |
| **P2 "Ignore for now"** | everything else |

Every row carries a machine-generated `reason` list, for example `["CISA KEV", "likely under-rated: CNA MEDIUM → predicted HIGH (p=0.82)", "fix: 4.17.21"]`. Tune τ_high on val and record it in `DECISIONS.md`.

### 8.2 Label rule (Task A and Task B)

For a CVE with status Analyzed or Modified **and** a CNA v3.1 vector:
- the label is the NVD Primary vector if NVD wrote one;
- otherwise the label is the CNA vector, because NVD reviewed it and kept it.

**Use `isinstance(x, str)` checks, not truthiness.** A NaN-is-truthy bug already happened once and silently mislabelled about 40% of rows. Keep the regression test in §14.

**Known caveat** (put it in the post): in 2026, NVD writes its own score much less often. Some "kept" labels may reflect lower review effort rather than agreement. Mitigation: report val (2025-H2) and test (2026) separately, and add a sensitivity analysis on Jan–Feb 2024, when NVD wrote its own score for about 91% of CVEs.

### 8.3 Splits (time-based, never random)

| Split | Rule |
|---|---|
| `train` | published before 2025-07-01 |
| `val` | 2025-07-01 to 2025-12-31 |
| `test` | 2026-01-01 onwards |
| `deferred_unlabeled` | status Deferred with a CNA vector. This is the population the product scores. |

Bump-up base rates: train 18%, val 23%, test 9%.

### 8.4 Leakage rules (enforce in `features.py`, test in `tests/test_features.py`)

Never use any of the following as features:
- `status`, because NVD prioritises KEV CVEs
- `nvd_vector`
- NVD's CWE (`weaknesses[type=Primary]`)
- NVD reference tags (NVD adds these during analysis)
- `configurations` / `has_cpe`
- `kev_date` (it is a report field only)

Features must be computable for a Deferred CVE on the day it was published. Fit TF-IDF and SVD vocabularies on `train` only.

- API key in `PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY` **[HUMAN]**.
- Prices: $0.15/M input, $0.03/M cached input, $0.50/M output (as of 2026-10-15; **VERIFY**).

**Agent shape.**
- The model receives the structured scan JSON. Rows are already prioritised; the model never sets priorities.
- Tools, if the endpoint supports OpenAI tool calling (**VERIFY**; otherwise inline everything):
  - `get_cve(cve_id)` returns the description, CNA vector and predicted vector
  - `explain_flag(cve_id)` returns the top TabPFN or HGB feature contributions (permutation importance or SHAP on HGB)
  - `similar_cves(cve_id, k=3)` returns past CVEs with the same CNA and CWE, together with what NVD did

**Output.** Markdown:
1. a 3-line summary
2. a P0 table, then P1, then a collapsed P2 section
3. one plain-English reason per CVE
4. a footer stating that the scores are estimates, with the data dates

**Guardrail.**
- Extract every CVE ID and every number in the output and check that each appears in the input JSON.
- If the check fails, retry once. If it fails again, fall back to the Jinja template report.
- Log the pass rate.

**Cost logging.** Write tokens, latency and dollars per call to `results/costs.jsonl` through `costs.py`.

| Endpoint | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `POST /scan` | Multipart: lockfile upload or pasted text. Returns `{rows, report_md, costs, data_as_of}`. |
| `GET /cve/{id}` | Single-CVE second opinion |
| `GET /feed/latest.csv` | The open data feed |
| `GET /health` | Health check |

Limits: uploads up to 2 MB; rate-limit by IP.

### 11.6 Web page (`web/index.html`)

- One static page served by FastAPI.
- A textarea or file drop → POST `/scan` → render the report.
- Show a "data as of" date and an "estimates, not official" banner.
- No framework is required. Keep it clean and readable on mobile.

### 11.7 LLM backends (`llm/backends.py`)

All backends share one interface: `predict_vectors(rows) -> list[str]`.

| Backend | How it works |
|---|---|
| `VLLMBackend` | OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` on the DigitalOcean GPU Droplet, `model="patchsloth"` |
| `TinkerBackend` | Tinker sampling client with the saved weights |
| `NullBackend` | Returns the CNA vector; used with `--no-llm` |

Choose the backend with `PATCHSLOTH_LLM_BACKEND`.

**App Platform** (CPU, small instance):
- Docker image of the FastAPI app.
- At start-up, downloads the latest `second_opinion.parquet` from a DigitalOcean Space or the repo's GitHub release.

## 13. Configuration and secrets

`.env.example` lists:
- `TINKER_API_KEY`
- `PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY`
- `PATCHSLOTH_LLM_BACKEND`
- `VLLM_BASE_URL`, `VLLM_API_KEY`
- `OSV_SCANNER_LOCAL_DB_CACHE_DIRECTORY`
- `DO_SPACES_*` (if used)

**Never commit secrets.** Entire stores session transcripts in git (`entire/checkpoints/v1`) and redacts secrets only on a best-effort basis. Keep keys in `.env` (gitignored), and never paste keys into the chat with the agent.

## 14. Testing

Run `pytest -q`. It must pass offline.

| Test file | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `test_cvss.py` | Base scores for at least 6 known vectors (9.8, 6.1, 5.5, 9.0, plus a scope-changed and a zero-impact vector); severity bands |
| `test_label_rule.py` | Analyzed with NVD vector → label is NVD; Analyzed without → label is CNA; Deferred → none; NaN inputs never produce a label (**regression for the NaN bug**) |
| `test_features.py` | The feature list contains no forbidden columns (§8.4); train/serve feature parity on a fixture row |
| `test_prompt.py` | `parse_output` handles valid JSON, extra text, invalid values and empty output |
| `test_scan.py` | Fixture lockfiles → expected CVE set (fallback matcher; osv-scanner test is skipped if the binary is missing) |
| `test_priority.py` | Each bucket rule |
| `test_report_guardrail.py` | An injected fake CVE or number is caught |

# Patch Sloth: Build Specification

> **For Claude Code.** This is the single source of truth for the project.
> - Read the whole document before writing code.
> - Work milestone by milestone (§15), and check each milestone's acceptance criteria before moving on.
> - Stop and ask the human whenever you reach a step tagged **[HUMAN]** (full list in §16).
> - Do not invent third-party API names. Where this spec says **VERIFY**, read the linked docs (or `--help`) first, then write the code.
> - Keep every decision you make in `DECISIONS.md`, one line each, with the date and the reason. The write-up depends on it.

---

## 1. One-paragraph summary

Since April 2026, NIST's National Vulnerability Database (NVD) no longer analyses every CVE. Many CVEs are marked **Deferred**. For those, the only severity score is the one supplied by the **CNA**, the organisation that reported the vulnerability (often the vendor itself). In the years when NVD still reviewed CNA scores, it changed the CNA's CVSS vector about 4 in 10 times. When it changed the severity band, it raised it about 3 times more often than it lowered it.

**Patch Sloth** gives a maintainer the missing second opinion for the CVEs in *their own* lockfile:
- It predicts what an independent NVD-style reviewer would likely have scored.
- It flags CVEs that are probably under-rated.
- It writes a one-minute "patch now / this month / ignore" report.

It is built for the DEV Hacktoberfest 2026 Open-Source AI Challenge, Week 3 ("Slow and Steady": build something with open-source AI that rewards laziness). The due date is **Oct 25, 2026, 11:59 PM PDT**, which is Mon Oct 26, 12:29 PM IST.

## 2. Evidence already measured (cite these; recompute in M1)

These numbers come from NVD records 2021–2026, taken from the fkie-cad mirror on 2026-10-21.

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| 2026 CVE IDs so far | 78,297 |
| Deferred | 28,518 (36%) |
| Deferred, Awaiting Analysis or Received (no NVD analysis) | 41,907 (54%) |
| Deferred per month (2026 IDs) | Mar 1,382 → Aug 5,196 → Sep 5,629 |
| Deferred CVEs with some CVSS score | 99.4% (almost all supplied by the CNA) |
| Deferred CVEs with an NVD score | 1.5% |
| Deferred CVEs with CPE configurations | 0 |
| 2024: NVD wrote its own vector on CNA-scored CVEs | 16,741 of 26,465. It changed the CNA vector in 11,252 (43% of all) and changed the severity band in 6,489. |
| 2025: when NVD changed the score, the score went up vs down | 6,419 vs 2,009 |
| Most disputed CVSS fields (2025) | C/I/A, disputed in 48–56% of the pairs where both NVD and the CNA scored. AV is disputed in only about 6%. |
| Biggest scorers of Deferred CVEs | VulDB, Patchstack, CISA-ADP (Vulnrichment), VulnCheck, GitHub, Wordfence |
| NVD writes its own score, share by month | 2024: 47–91% → 2026-H2: 11–13%. When it does, it differs from the CNA 80–95% of the time. |
| Total labelled dataset | 239,058 non-rejected CVEs. Splits: train 80,098 / val 11,655 / test 30,706. Deferred and unlabelled: 48,979. |

**Honesty framing (required in all copy):**
- NVD is not ground truth. NVD tends to score the worst case. Daniel Stenberg of curl has argued that NVD inflates severity ([source](https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2023/03/06/nvd-makes-up-vulnerability-severity-levels/)).
- The product therefore says *"an independent NVD-style reviewer would likely rate this higher"*. It must never say *"the vendor is wrong"*.
- All outputs are **estimates for triage, not official scores**.

## 3. Goals and non-goals

**Goals**
1. A reproducible dataset and evaluation that judges can trust: time-based splits, baselines, confidence intervals and significance tests.
2. A Task-A model: a Tinker LoRA fine-tune of an open-weight model that predicts the NVD-style CVSS v3.1 vector.
3. A Task-B model: TabPFN, predicting P(NVD would raise the CNA's severity band). It also stacks the LLM's output with tabular features.
4. A product: a CLI, a web page and an API. Input is a lockfile; output is a report written by Ultramarine.
5. Deployment on DigitalOcean.
6. A daily open data feed: a second-opinion CSV covering every Deferred CVE.
7. A DEV post that explains the work, with charts and honest limits.

**Non-goals (say so in the post)**
- Generating CPE (affected-product lists). This is future work.
- Beating EPSS at predicting exploitation. EPSS is used only as an input field.
- CVSS v4.0. We target v3.1 only, because that is what most CNAs and NVD provide.
- Ecosystems beyond npm and PyPI.

## 4. Partner technology mapping

| Partner | Role in Patch Sloth | Evidence to show in the post |
|---|---|---|
| **Tinker** (Thinking Machines) | LoRA SFT of `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` for Task A, using about 30k examples for 1 epoch. Also hosts base-model zero-shot sampling. | Base vs fine-tuned: JSON validity, per-field accuracy, bump-up recall and precision, McNemar against copy-CNA. Training loss curve. Cost. |
| **TabPFN** (Prior Labs) | Task B classifier, plus the stacking "decision layer" inside the triage agent. Prior Labs favours TabPFN inside a wider prediction agent. | PR-AUC with CIs against logistic regression and HistGBT. A scaling curve over `n_train`. Calibration plot. |
| **DigitalOcean** | App Platform hosts the FastAPI app and UI. A GPU Droplet runs vLLM with the LoRA adapter, for on-demand second opinions and the nightly feed job. | Architecture diagram, latency, hourly cost, screenshots. |
| **Ultramarine 1 Flash** (Paper Instruments) | Report writer, with tool calling if supported. Also a frontier-style zero-shot baseline on 1k test CVEs. | Cost per report (tokens × price), guardrail pass rate, baseline comparison. |
| **Entire** | Records every Claude Code session that builds this repo, on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. | Link to the sessions in the post, and use `entire checkpoint explain` to show why key code exists. |
| *(optional)* **DevRelay** | Saves an agent transcript to DEV and embeds it in the post. The submission template asks for this. | An embedded transcript in the post. |

Do not add more partners, for example simply to inflate the count. Four done well, plus Entire, is the strategy.

## 5. Architecture

```
                         ┌───────────── offline / nightly (GPU) ─────────────┐
 NVD mirror (fkie-cad) ──►  build_dataset ─► cves.parquet ─► Task A (Tinker LoRA, vLLM)
 CISA KEV  ─────────────►                         │            Task B (TabPFN)
 EPSS (daily CSV) ──────►                         ▼                    │
                                       feed/second_opinion.parquet ◄───┘
                                       (every Deferred/unanalysed CVE:
                                        cna_vector, predicted_vector, p_bump, epss, kev)
                         └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                                  │ (uploaded nightly)
 user lockfile ─► osv-scanner (offline DB) ─► CVE IDs ─► lookup in feed ──► priority rules
                                                  │  (not in feed? → on-demand:
                                                  │   vLLM second opinion + HGB fallback)
                                                  ▼
                                     Ultramarine report agent ─► report.md / JSON / web page
```

**Key design decision:**
- TabPFN is too slow to refit on a CPU web server for each request.
- So **all bump probabilities are precomputed nightly** for every Deferred, Awaiting Analysis and Received CVE, and stored in the feed.
- The web app only looks values up.
- CVEs newer than the last feed get an on-demand LLM second opinion plus the fast HistGBT fallback, and are labelled as such.

## 6. Repository layout (target)

```
patch-sloth/
  SPEC.md  PLAN.md  DECISIONS.md  README.md  CLAUDE.md  requirements.txt  .env.example
  patchsloth/
    __init__.py
    cvss.py            # EXISTS: parse/to_vector/base_score/severity (tested vs known vectors)
    metrics.py         # EXISTS: evaluate(), mcnemar()
    config.py          # paths, thresholds, model names, prices (read from env)
    data/nvd.py        # loading feeds, label rule, splits (refactor of scripts/02)
    data/epss.py       # download + time-matched lookup
    features.py        # tabular features shared by train and serve (single source!)
    llm/prompt.py      # SYSTEM prompt + prompt(row) + parse_output()  (shared by train/serve)
    llm/backends.py    # VLLMBackend (OpenAI-compatible), TinkerBackend, NullBackend
    tabular.py         # train/predict TabPFN, HGB fallback, calibration, threshold
    scan.py            # osv-scanner wrapper + fallback GHSA matcher
    priority.py        # deterministic priority rules (§11.3)
    report.py          # Ultramarine agent + guardrail + template fallback
    costs.py           # token/latency/cost logging -> results/costs.jsonl
    feed.py            # nightly feed build
    api.py             # FastAPI app
    cli.py             # `patchsloth` entry point (Typer)
  scripts/             # EXISTS 01–07; add 08_backlog_charts.py, 09_frontier_baseline.py, 10_error_analysis.py
  web/index.html       # single page: paste/upload lockfile -> report
  tests/               # pytest; fixtures/ with small lockfiles and NVD records
  deploy/              # Dockerfile, do-app.yaml, vllm-droplet.sh
  .github/workflows/feed.yml   # optional nightly feed refresh
  results/             # metrics JSON, charts PNG, costs.jsonl (committed)
  data/                # gitignored
```

**What already exists:**
- `patchsloth/cvss.py` and `patchsloth/metrics.py`
- `scripts/01_download.sh` to `07_tabpfn_bump.py`
- `PLAN.md` and `README.md`

Scripts 01–04 and 07 (in `hgb`/`logreg` mode) have been run successfully. Scripts 05 and 06 were written but not yet run, because they need Tinker credentials. Refactor shared logic into the package, but keep the scripts as thin entry points.

## 7. Data sources

| Source | URL | Licence | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| NVD JSON 2.0, yearly | `https://github.com/fkie-cad/nvd-json-data-feeds/releases/latest/download/CVE-<YEAR>.json.xz` (2021–2026) | public domain | everything |
| CISA KEV | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cisagov/kev-data/develop/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json` | public domain | report field and feature |
| EPSS | `https://epss.empiricalsecurity.com/epss_scores-current.csv.gz`; history at `epss_scores-YYYY-MM-DD.csv.gz` (**VERIFY**: the host moved from epss.cyentia.com in 2025) | FIRST/Empirical | report field only |
| GitHub Advisory DB | `git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/github/advisory-database` then `sparse-checkout set advisories/github-reviewed` | CC-BY 4.0 | fallback matcher |
| OSV via osv-scanner | `osv-scanner` v2 binary with an offline DB cache | Apache-2.0 | lockfile → vulns |

The NVD record fields used are the same as in `scripts/02_build_dataset.py`:
- `vulnStatus`, `published`, `sourceIdentifier`, `descriptions[lang=en]`
- `metrics.cvssMetricV31[type=Primary|Secondary]`
- `weaknesses[type=Secondary]` (only the CNA's CWE: NVD's own CWE is not available at serve time)
- `references[].url`, `configurations`, `metrics.cvssMetricV40`

The CISA-ADP source UUID is `134c704f-9b21-4f2e-91b3-4a467353bcc0`.

## 8. Dataset, label rule, splits, leakage rules

**Honesty framing (required in all copy):**
- NVD is not ground truth. NVD tends to score the worst case. Daniel Stenberg of curl has argued that NVD inflates severity ([source](https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2023/03/06/nvd-makes-up-vulnerability-severity-levels/)).
- The product therefore says *"an independent NVD-style reviewer would likely rate this higher"*. It must never say *"the vendor is wrong"*.
- All outputs are **estimates for triage, not official scores**.

## 3. Goals and non-goals

**Goals**
1. A reproducible dataset and evaluation that judges can trust: time-based splits, baselines, confidence intervals and significance tests.
2. A Task-A model: a Tinker LoRA fine-tune of an open-weight model that predicts the NVD-style CVSS v3.1 vector.
3. A Task-B model: TabPFN, predicting P(NVD would raise the CNA's severity band). It also stacks the LLM's output with tabular features.
4. A product: a CLI, a web page and an API. Input is a lockfile; output is a report written by Ultramarine.
5. Deployment on DigitalOcean.
6. A daily open data feed: a second-opinion CSV covering every Deferred CVE.
7. A DEV post that explains the work, with charts and honest limits.

**Non-goals (say so in the post)**
- Generating CPE (affected-product lists). This is future work.
- Beating EPSS at predicting exploitation. EPSS is used only as an input field.
- CVSS v4.0. We target v3.1 only, because that is what most CNAs and NVD provide.
- Ecosystems beyond npm and PyPI.

## 4. Partner technology mapping

| Partner | Role in Patch Sloth | Evidence to show in the post |
|---|---|---|
| **Tinker** (Thinking Machines) | LoRA SFT of `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` for Task A, using about 30k examples for 1 epoch. Also hosts base-model zero-shot sampling. | Base vs fine-tuned: JSON validity, per-field accuracy, bump-up recall and precision, McNemar against copy-CNA. Training loss curve. Cost. |
| **TabPFN** (Prior Labs) | Task B classifier, plus the stacking "decision layer" inside the triage agent. Prior Labs favours TabPFN inside a wider prediction agent. | PR-AUC with CIs against logistic regression and HistGBT. A scaling curve over `n_train`. Calibration plot. |
| **DigitalOcean** | App Platform hosts the FastAPI app and UI. A GPU Droplet runs vLLM with the LoRA adapter, for on-demand second opinions and the nightly feed job. | Architecture diagram, latency, hourly cost, screenshots. |
| **Ultramarine 1 Flash** (Paper Instruments) | Report writer, with tool calling if supported. Also a frontier-style zero-shot baseline on 1k test CVEs. | Cost per report (tokens × price), guardrail pass rate, baseline comparison. |
| **Entire** | Records every Claude Code session that builds this repo, on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. | Link to the sessions in the post, and use `entire checkpoint explain` to show why key code exists. |
| *(optional)* **DevRelay** | Saves an agent transcript to DEV and embeds it in the post. The submission template asks for this. | An embedded transcript in the post. |

Do not add more partners, for example simply to inflate the count. Four done well, plus Entire, is the strategy.

## 5. Architecture

```
                         ┌───────────── offline / nightly (GPU) ─────────────┐
 NVD mirror (fkie-cad) ──►  build_dataset ─► cves.parquet ─► Task A (Tinker LoRA, vLLM)
 CISA KEV  ─────────────►                         │            Task B (TabPFN)
 EPSS (daily CSV) ──────►                         ▼                    │
                                       feed/second_opinion.parquet ◄───┘
                                       (every Deferred/unanalysed CVE:
                                        cna_vector, predicted_vector, p_bump, epss, kev)
                         └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                                  │ (uploaded nightly)
 user lockfile ─► osv-scanner (offline DB) ─► CVE IDs ─► lookup in feed ──► priority rules
                                                  │  (not in feed? → on-demand:
                                                  │   vLLM second opinion + HGB fallback)
                                                  ▼
                                     Ultramarine report agent ─► report.md / JSON / web page
```

**Key design decision:**
- TabPFN is too slow to refit on a CPU web server for each request.
- So **all bump probabilities are precomputed nightly** for every Deferred, Awaiting Analysis and Received CVE, and stored in the feed.
- The web app only looks values up.
- CVEs newer than the last feed get an on-demand LLM second opinion plus the fast HistGBT fallback, and are labelled as such.

"""Serve-time stacked model: TabPFN-3.5 + fine-tuned-LLM features, trained on the 10k out-of-SFT stack_train rows
(seed 0), with Bands and the gate threshold. Saved to data/models/bump_stack.joblib for
`patchsloth feed build --model stack --llm --backend precomputed`.
- Gate t: chosen in M4 on the last 3 months of val (results/gated_override.json, seed 0). Verified here: this model's
  val/test predictions equal the M4 seed-0 stack's, so t applies unchanged.
- Bands: label-free quantiles of this model's p_bump over the Deferred CVEs that have an LLM vector (scripts/16).
  Isotonic on the last 3 months of val (rows with LLM predictions).
Usage: python scripts/17_stacked_model.py   (after scripts/16)"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from patchsloth import tabular  # noqa: E402
from patchsloth.features import LLM_INPUT, FeatureBuilder  # noqa: E402

R = Path("results")
df = pd.read_parquet("data/cves.parquet")
df = df[df.split.isin(["train", "val", "test", "deferred_unlabeled"])].copy()
v = {}
for s in ["stack_train", "val", "test", "unanalysed"]:
    v.update(json.loads((R / f"llm_vectors_ft_{s}.json").read_text()))
df[LLM_INPUT] = df.cve.map(v)
has = df[LLM_INPUT].notna()
train = df.split == "train"
fb = FeatureBuilder(with_llm=True).fit(df[df.split.isin(["train", "val", "test"]) & train])
X, y = fb.transform(df), df.bump_up
idx = df[train & has].index
clf = tabular.fit("tabpfn", X.loc[idx], y.loc[idx], seed=0)

m_eval = (df.split.isin(["val", "test"]) & has).to_numpy()
p_eval = pd.Series(tabular.predict_proba(clf, X[m_eval]), index=df.cve[m_eval])
ref = pd.read_parquet("data/m4/tabpfn_llm_stack_s0.parquet").set_index("cve").p
diff = float(np.abs(p_eval.loc[ref.index].to_numpy() - ref.to_numpy()).max())
print("max |p - M4 seed-0 stack| =", diff)
assert diff < 1e-3, "model differs from the M4 stack: the gate threshold would not apply"

m_def = (df.split == "deferred_unlabeled").to_numpy() & has.to_numpy()
val = df.split == "val"
start = str((pd.Timestamp(df.published[val].max()) - pd.DateOffset(months=3)).date())
m_rec = (val & has & (df.published >= start)).to_numpy()
p_def = tabular.predict_proba(clf, X[m_def])
bands = tabular.Bands(p_def, tabular.predict_proba(clf, X[m_rec]), y[m_rec].astype(int),
                      val_window=f"val with LLM predictions, published >= {start} (n={int(m_rec.sum())})")
model = tabular.BumpModel(fb, clf, "stack", bands)
gate = json.loads((R / "gated_override.json").read_text())["seeds"]["0"]["chosen_on_val_last3m"]
model.gate_t = float(gate["t"])
print("saved", model.save())

# evidence on the 8k eval test rows (reported only)
m_t = (df.split == "test").to_numpy() & has.to_numpy()
pt = tabular.predict_proba(clf, X[m_t])
yt = y[m_t].astype(int).to_numpy()
b = bands.band(pt)
hi = pt >= bands.tau_high
out = dict(model="stack (TabPFN-3.5 + LLM features, 10k stack_train, seed 0)", gate_t=model.gate_t,
           gate_rule="chosen on the last 3 months of val (M4, seed 0)", max_abs_diff_vs_m4=diff, **bands.as_dict(),
           n_deferred_with_llm=int(m_def.sum()), n_deferred_all=int((df.split == "deferred_unlabeled").sum()),
           test_eval_rows=dict(n=int(m_t.sum()), base_rate=float(yt.mean()),
                               bands={k: dict(share=float((b == k).mean()), n=int((b == k).sum()),
                                              observed_bump_rate=float(yt[b == k].mean())) for k in tabular.BANDS},
                               at_tau_high=dict(flag_rate=float(hi.mean()), precision=float(yt[hi].mean()),
                                                recall=float(yt[hi].sum() / yt.sum())),
                               gated_override=gate["test"], gated_vs_copy_cna=gate["test_vs_copy_cna"]))
(R / "serving_stack.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1))
print(json.dumps({k: out[k] for k in ["gate_t", "tau", "tau_high", "tau_possible", "n_deferred_with_llm"]}),
      json.dumps(out["test_eval_rows"]["bands"]))

"""M4 experiments: fit every Task-B configuration with 3 seeds and save per-row val/test predictions.
Analysis (paired bootstrap, tables) is in scripts/13_final_table.py.

Training rows per config (seed s draws the subsample AND seeds the model):
  *_full      all train rows (80,098)            *_50k / *_30k  random train subsample
  *_recent    train rows published >= 2024-01-01 (TabPFN: subsample to 50k if larger)
  *_stack     the 10k out-of-SFT stack_train rows (the only train rows with LLM predictions)
  *_llm_stack the same rows, plus the fine-tuned LLM's features (SPEC §9.2 stacking)
  hgb_noes_*  HGB with early stopping off (diagnostic for the 30k-vs-80k anomaly)
Tabular configs are scored on all val/test rows; LLM configs only on rows with LLM predictions (the M3 eval rows).
Resumable: existing data/m4/<config>_s<seed>.parquet files are skipped. Progress: data/m4/progress.log.
Usage: python scripts/12_m4_experiments.py [--only tabpfn_50k,hgb_full] [--seeds 0,1,2]"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from patchsloth import tabular  # noqa: E402
from patchsloth.features import LLM_INPUT, FeatureBuilder  # noqa: E402

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--only", default="")
ap.add_argument("--seeds", default="0,1,2")
a = ap.parse_args()
OUT = Path("data/m4")
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
LOG = OUT / "progress.log"

# (name, model, train rows, n cap or None, with LLM features, early stopping)
CONFIGS = [
    ("lr_full", "logreg", "train", None, False),
    ("hgb_full", "hgb", "train", None, False),
    ("hgb_50k", "hgb", "train", 50000, False),
    ("hgb_5k", "hgb", "train", 5000, False),
    ("hgb_10k", "hgb", "train", 10000, False),
    ("hgb_30k", "hgb", "train", 30000, False),
    ("hgb_recent", "hgb", "recent", None, False),
    ("hgb_noes_full", "hgb_noes", "train", None, False),
    ("hgb_noes_30k", "hgb_noes", "train", 30000, False),
    ("hgb_stack", "hgb", "stack", None, False),
    ("hgb_llm_stack", "hgb", "stack", None, True),
    ("tabpfn_stack", "tabpfn", "stack", None, False),
    ("tabpfn_llm_stack", "tabpfn", "stack", None, True),
    ("tabpfn_5k", "tabpfn", "train", 5000, False),
    ("tabpfn_10k", "tabpfn", "train", 10000, False),
    ("tabpfn_30k", "tabpfn", "train", 30000, False),
    ("tabpfn_50k", "tabpfn", "train", 50000, False),
    ("tabpfn_recent", "tabpfn", "recent", 50000, False),
]
only = set(filter(None, a.only.split(",")))
seeds = [int(s) for s in a.seeds.split(",")]

df = pd.read_parquet("data/cves.parquet")
df = df[df.split.isin(["train", "val", "test"])].copy()
llm = {}
for split in ["stack_train", "val", "test"]:
    llm.update(json.loads(Path(f"results/llm_vectors_ft_{split}.json").read_text()))
df[LLM_INPUT] = df.cve.map(llm)
has_llm = df[LLM_INPUT].notna()
train = df.split == "train"
pools = {"train": train, "recent": train & (df.published >= "2024-01-01"), "stack": train & has_llm}
fb_tab = FeatureBuilder().fit(df[train])
fb_llm = FeatureBuilder(with_llm=True).fit(df[train])
X_tab, X_llm = fb_tab.transform(df), fb_llm.transform(df)
y = df.bump_up.astype(int)


def log(msg):
    line = f"{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')} {msg}"
    print(line, flush=True)
    with open(LOG, "a") as f:
        f.write(line + "\n")


todo = [(c, s) for c in CONFIGS for s in seeds if (not only or c[0] in only)
        and not (OUT / f"{c[0]}_s{s}.parquet").exists()]
log(f"start: {len(todo)} runs to do")
for i, ((name, model, pool, cap, with_llm), seed) in enumerate(todo, 1):
    if model == "logreg" and seed != seeds[0] and cap is None:
        continue  # deterministic on the full pool: one run is enough
    t0 = time.time()
    rows = df[pools[pool]]
    idx = rows.sample(n=min(cap, len(rows)), random_state=seed).index if cap else rows.index
    X = X_llm if with_llm else X_tab
    if model == "hgb_noes":
        from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier
        clf = HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=400, learning_rate=0.05, early_stopping=False,
                                             random_state=seed).fit(X.loc[idx].fillna(0).values, y.loc[idx].values)
    else:
        clf = tabular.fit(model, X.loc[idx], y.loc[idx], seed=seed)
    score = df.split.isin(["val", "test"]) & (has_llm if with_llm else True)
    p = tabular.predict_proba(clf, X[score])
    pd.DataFrame({"cve": df.cve[score].to_numpy(), "split": df.split[score].to_numpy(),
                  "published": df.published[score].to_numpy(), "y": y[score].to_numpy(), "p": p}) \
        .to_parquet(OUT / f"{name}_s{seed}.parquet", index=False)
    log(f"[{i}/{len(todo)}] {name} seed {seed}: n_train {len(idx)}, scored {int(score.sum())}, "
        f"{time.time() - t0:.0f}s")
log("done")
"""M4 add-ons.
(1) Every model on the SAME 1,000 test rows Ultramarine was scored on (results/frontier_subsample.json):
    Task A (vectors) for copy-CNA, TF-IDF+LR, base Qwen, fine-tuned Qwen, Ultramarine; Task B (bump ranking) for
    the tabular/stacked models. Plus cost per 1k CVEs from results/costs.jsonl.
(2) Gated override: final vector = fine-tuned LLM vector if stacked p_bump >= t, else the CNA vector. t is swept

def vecs(name, split):
    if name == "tfidf_lr":

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- (1) same 1k rows + cost
sub = json.loads((R / "frontier_subsample.json").read_text())["cves"]
d = df.loc[sub]
task_a = {}
copy_res, ok_copy = evaluate(d, list(d.cna_vector), n_boot=N_BOOT)

    res["mcnemar_vs_copy_cna_severity"] = mcnemar(ok, ok_copy)
    task_a[name] = res
y1k = d.bump_up.astype(int).to_numpy()
task_b = {"copy_cna": dict(pr_auc=float(y1k.mean()), note="constant score: PR-AUC = base rate")}

    pr = [average_precision_score(y1k, m4(name, s).loc[sub].to_numpy()) for s in SEEDS
          if (M4 / f"{name}_s{s}.parquet").exists()]

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |
